$comment: Version 2 of the ontology, proposed for comparison with ontology.json. It keeps every dimension and category id of ontology.json, adds categories where a dimension had gaps, and gives every category a results chain: short-term, medium-term and long-term outcomes with three predefined indicators each.

dimensions.name: Political & governance
dimensions.definition: Changes involving political institutions, policy, governance, regulation, or public decision-making.

categories.name: Advocacy & policy influence
categories.definition: Efforts or changes intended to influence laws, policies, political agendas, or public decision-makers.
include: policy recommendations
government engagement
legislative or regulatory influence
adoption of a standard or guideline
exclude: general public awareness without a policy objective
internal organisational strategy
questions: What policy or legislative change did this work seek to bring about, and was it adopted?
Which government bodies or decision-makers were engaged, and what did they commit to?
What evidence shows a recommendation was taken up in law, regulation, or official guidance?
How is the influence of this work on the policy agenda measured or reported?

outcomes.statement: Decision-makers receive the work's proposals and the issue reaches the policy agenda.

indicators.name: Policy recommendations submitted
indicators.question: How many policy recommendations, proposals or draft texts were submitted to government or legislators?

indicators.name: Decision-makers engaged
indicators.question: Which ministries, legislative committees or officials were engaged on the proposals?

indicators.name: Issue placed on the official agenda
indicators.question: Was the issue taken up in a hearing, committee, cabinet meeting, consultation or other official agenda?

outcomes.statement: Recommendations are adopted into law, regulation, official guidance or budget decisions.

indicators.name: Share of recommendations adopted
indicators.question: Of the recommendations submitted, how many were adopted by the responsible authority, as a count or a share?

indicators.name: Stage reached by the policy instrument
indicators.question: How far did the targeted law, regulation, guideline or policy get?

indicators.name: Formal commitments made
indicators.question: What did decision-makers formally commit to, such as a review, a vote, a deadline or a budget allocation?

outcomes.statement: Adopted policies are funded, implemented and enforced, and change conditions for the people they target.

indicators.name: Adopted policy implemented and enforced
indicators.question: Is the adopted policy being implemented and enforced, for example through regulations, staff, monitoring or sanctions?

indicators.name: Sustained public funding
indicators.question: Is there a recurring public budget allocation or financing that sustains the policy?

indicators.name: Change for the target population
indicators.question: What change in the target population's conditions is attributed to the adopted policy?

categories.name: Governance & institutional capacity
categories.definition: Changes in the capability, accountability, transparency, or integrity of public institutions.
include: public administration reform
anti-corruption measures
transparency and audit
civil service capability
exclude: private-sector corporate governance
purely financial performance of an institution
questions: How did the capacity of the responsible public institution change as a result of the intervention?
What accountability, audit, or transparency mechanisms were introduced or strengthened?
Which indicators track improvements in governance quality or institutional performance?
What evidence is reported on corruption, integrity, or misuse of public resources?

outcomes.statement: Public officials gain skills and institutions gain new systems, procedures or oversight bodies.

indicators.name: Public officials trained
indicators.question: How many public officials or civil servants were trained?

indicators.name: Systems, procedures or bodies introduced
indicators.question: Which new systems, procedures, committees or oversight bodies were introduced in public institutions?

indicators.name: Audit or assessment carried out
indicators.question: Was an audit, review or assessment of the institution or programme carried out?

outcomes.statement: New practices become routine: reports are published, audit findings are acted on and rules are applied.

indicators.name: Regular publication of public reports
indicators.question: Which fiscal, procurement, audit or performance reports are now published, and how often?

indicators.name: Audit recommendations acted on
indicators.question: What share of audit or oversight recommendations was implemented by the institution?

indicators.name: Governance rules adopted
indicators.question: Which laws, standards or rules on procurement, financial management or integrity were adopted?

outcomes.statement: Institutions perform better, misuse of public resources falls and trust in institutions grows.

indicators.name: Change in a governance quality score
indicators.question: How did a governance, transparency or public financial management score change (for example PEFA, CPI or WGI)?

indicators.name: Change in irregularities or corruption cases
indicators.question: How did reported irregularities, corruption cases or misuse of public funds change?

indicators.name: Public trust in institutions
indicators.question: How did public trust in, or satisfaction with, the institution change?

categories.name: Civic participation & representation
categories.definition: Changes in how citizens participate in, or are represented within, public decision-making.
include: electoral participation
public consultation
civil society space
representation of under-represented groups
exclude: consumer market behaviour
employee engagement inside an organisation
questions: How did citizen or community participation in decision-making change?
Which groups gained or lost representation in governing or consultative bodies?
What consultation processes were run, and how were their results used?
How is civic space or freedom of association reported to have changed?

outcomes.statement: Citizens and civil society take part in consultations and new participation channels open.

indicators.name: Consultations held
indicators.question: How many public consultations, hearings or participatory meetings were held?

indicators.name: People or organisations taking part
indicators.question: How many citizens or civil society organisations took part in consultations or participatory processes?

indicators.name: Groups consulted
indicators.question: Which stakeholder groups were consulted, such as civil society, the private sector, women or minorities?

outcomes.statement: Under-represented groups take part in decision-making bodies and citizen input shapes decisions.

indicators.name: Share of under-represented groups in decision bodies
indicators.question: What share of members or participants in councils, committees or consultative bodies are women or other under-represented groups?

indicators.name: Citizen input reflected in decisions
indicators.question: How was input from consultations used in the final plan, policy or budget?

indicators.name: Participation mechanism made permanent
indicators.question: Was a participation mechanism, such as a council, committee or participatory budget, made permanent in rules or law?

outcomes.statement: Citizens participate more in public life and civic space is protected.

indicators.name: Change in electoral turnout
indicators.question: How did voter turnout or electoral participation change?

indicators.name: Change in representation in elected office
indicators.question: How did the representation of women or other under-represented groups in elected office, such as parliament or elected local councils, change?

indicators.name: Change in civic space
indicators.question: How did the space for civil society, a free press or freedom of association change?

categories.name: Elections & electoral integrity
categories.definition: Changes in how elections are administered, contested, observed and accepted.
include: election administration and management bodies
voter registration and voter education
election observation and dispute resolution
campaign and political party finance rules
exclude: voter turnout and the representation of groups, which belong to civic participation & representation
party advocacy on a single policy issue
questions: How did the administration of elections or the capacity of the election management body change?
What changes to voter registration, voter education or access to polling are reported?
How were electoral disputes, irregularities or observer findings handled?
What rules on campaign or political party finance were introduced or enforced?

outcomes.statement: Election bodies, observers and voters are prepared for the election.

indicators.name: Election officials and observers trained
indicators.question: How many election officials, poll workers or observers were trained?

indicators.name: Voters registered
indicators.question: How many voters were newly registered or had their registration updated?

indicators.name: Reach of voter education
indicators.question: Who was reached by voter education or information campaigns, and how many people?

outcomes.statement: Elections are run according to the rules, are observed, and disputes are settled through formal channels.

indicators.name: Observer assessment of the election
indicators.question: How did domestic or international observers assess the conduct of the election?

indicators.name: Electoral disputes resolved
indicators.question: What share of electoral complaints or disputes was resolved by the responsible body?

indicators.name: Stage reached by the electoral reform
indicators.question: How far did the targeted electoral law or reform get?

outcomes.statement: Elections are credible, their results are accepted and electoral institutions are trusted.

indicators.name: Election results accepted
indicators.question: Were the election results accepted by the main contestants without violent or prolonged dispute?

indicators.name: Change in an electoral integrity score
indicators.question: How did an electoral integrity or democracy score change (for example V-Dem, Perceptions of Electoral Integrity or Freedom House)?

indicators.name: Public trust in elections
indicators.question: How did public trust in elections or in the election management body change?

categories.name: Parliaments, parties & oversight
categories.definition: Changes in how legislatures and political parties make law, represent constituents and hold the executive to account.
include: parliamentary strengthening
committee scrutiny and budget oversight
political party development
constituency engagement by representatives
exclude: lobbying a legislature for a specific policy, which belongs to advocacy & policy influence
audit institutions and administrative oversight bodies, which belong to governance & institutional capacity
questions: How did the capacity of the legislature or its committees to draft and scrutinise legislation change?
What oversight of the executive, such as hearings, inquiries or budget scrutiny, is reported?
How did political parties change their internal organisation, programmes or candidate selection?
How do elected representatives engage with and report back to their constituents?

outcomes.statement: Legislators, parliamentary staff and parties gain skills, research support and procedures.

indicators.name: Legislators and staff trained
indicators.question: How many legislators, parliamentary staff or party officials were trained or supported?

indicators.name: Parliamentary services or procedures introduced
indicators.question: Which research services, procedures, committees or caucuses were set up in the legislature or in parties?

indicators.name: Oversight hearings held
indicators.question: How many oversight hearings, inquiries or committee sessions were held?

outcomes.statement: Committees scrutinise bills and budgets, and the executive responds to parliamentary oversight.

indicators.name: Bills or budgets amended after scrutiny
indicators.question: Which bills or budgets were amended as a result of committee scrutiny or parliamentary debate?

indicators.name: Executive responses to parliament
indicators.question: What share of parliamentary questions, recommendations or inquiry findings received a response from the executive?

indicators.name: Party reforms adopted
indicators.question: Which internal party reforms were adopted, such as candidate selection rules, quotas or policy programmes?

outcomes.statement: The legislature is an effective check on the executive and parties represent citizens.

indicators.name: Change in the legislature's check on the executive
indicators.question: How did the legislature's ability to check the executive change, for example through budget amendments, concluded inquiries or rejected appointments?

indicators.name: Change in a legislative effectiveness score
indicators.question: How did a score for legislative effectiveness or constraints on the executive change (for example V-Dem or the Bertelsmann Transformation Index)?

indicators.name: Public trust in parliament and parties
indicators.question: How did public trust in parliament or political parties change?

categories.name: Rule of law & justice institutions
categories.definition: Changes in the independence, capacity and performance of courts, prosecutors and other justice institutions.
include: judicial independence and appointments
court administration and case backlog
legal aid and dispute resolution services
justice sector reform
exclude: the rights and protection of specific at-risk people, which belong to protection & human rights; war crimes prosecutions, which belong to conduct of hostilities & IHL compliance
treaty ratification and compliance with international norms, which belong to legal frameworks & normative compliance
questions: How did the independence, staffing or capacity of courts and prosecution services change?
What change in case processing times, backlogs or clearance rates is reported?
Which justice sector reforms were adopted, and how far has their implementation got?
How did the availability and use of legal aid or dispute resolution services change?

outcomes.statement: Justice officials gain skills and new courts, services or case systems start operating.

indicators.name: Justice officials trained
indicators.question: How many judges, prosecutors, court staff or legal aid providers were trained?

indicators.name: Justice services established
indicators.question: Which courts, legal aid offices, case management systems or dispute resolution services were set up?

indicators.name: People receiving legal aid
indicators.question: How many people received legal aid, legal advice or mediation?

outcomes.statement: Cases move faster, reforms are adopted and court decisions are enforced.

indicators.name: Change in case processing
indicators.question: How did case processing time, backlog or clearance rate change?

indicators.name: Stage reached by the justice reform
indicators.question: How far did the targeted justice sector law or reform get?

indicators.name: Court decisions enforced
indicators.question: What share of court decisions or rulings was enforced or complied with?

outcomes.statement: Courts are independent, the law is applied equally and people trust the justice system.

indicators.name: Change in judicial independence
indicators.question: How did judicial independence change, for example in appointments, tenure or rulings against the government?

indicators.name: Change in a rule of law score
indicators.question: How did a rule of law score change (for example the WJP Rule of Law Index or the WGI rule of law indicator)?

indicators.name: Public trust in the justice system
indicators.question: How did public trust in, or satisfaction with, courts and the justice system change?

categories.name: Decentralisation & local governance
categories.definition: Changes in the powers, resources and responsiveness of subnational and local governments.
include: devolution of powers and functions
intergovernmental transfers and local revenue
municipal planning and management
local accountability mechanisms
exclude: national civil service reform, which belongs to governance & institutional capacity
the quality of a specific service such as water or schooling, which belongs to the social and education dimensions
questions: Which powers, functions or budgets were transferred to subnational or local governments?
How did the revenue, planning or management capacity of local governments change?
How do local governments respond to residents and account to them?
What evidence shows that local government performance changed after decentralisation?

outcomes.statement: Local governments receive support, trained staff and plans or budgets of their own.

indicators.name: Local governments supported
indicators.question: How many municipalities, districts or other local governments were supported?

indicators.name: Local officials trained
indicators.question: How many local government officials or councillors were trained?

indicators.name: Local plans and budgets prepared
indicators.question: Which local development plans, budgets or bylaws were prepared?

outcomes.statement: Functions and money move to local governments, and local revenue grows.

indicators.name: Functions devolved
indicators.question: Which functions, powers or staff were formally transferred to local governments?

indicators.name: Share of public spending managed locally
indicators.question: What share of public expenditure or revenue is managed by subnational or local governments?

indicators.name: Change in local own-source revenue
indicators.question: How did the revenue that local governments raise themselves change?

outcomes.statement: Local governments perform better, residents are more satisfied and the arrangement is permanent.

indicators.name: Change in local government performance
indicators.question: How did local government performance change, for example in an assessment score, budget execution or audit result?

indicators.name: Residents' satisfaction with local government
indicators.question: How did residents' satisfaction with, or trust in, local government change?

indicators.name: Decentralisation fixed in law
indicators.question: Is the decentralisation arrangement fixed in the constitution, in law or in a recurring transfer formula?

categories.name: Public finance & budget management
categories.definition: Changes in how public money is raised, budgeted, spent and controlled.
include: budget planning and credibility
tax administration and domestic revenue mobilisation
expenditure control and treasury management
public investment management
exclude: audit, anti-corruption and transparency mechanisms, which belong to governance & institutional capacity
growth, inflation and debt sustainability, which belong to macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
questions: How did budget planning, budget execution or expenditure control change?
What change in tax administration or domestic revenue collection is reported?
How are public investment projects selected, budgeted and monitored?
Which indicators track the credibility of the budget, such as the gap between planned and actual spending?

outcomes.statement: Finance ministries and tax authorities gain systems, trained staff and a diagnosis of weaknesses.

indicators.name: Financial management systems introduced
indicators.question: Which budget, treasury, tax or financial management information systems were introduced?

indicators.name: Finance and tax officials trained
indicators.question: How many budget, treasury or tax officials were trained?

indicators.name: Public finance assessment carried out
indicators.question: Was a public financial management or tax administration assessment, such as PEFA or TADAT, carried out?

outcomes.statement: Budgets are executed as approved, revenue collection improves and finance reforms are adopted.

indicators.name: Budget execution rate
indicators.question: What share of the approved budget was actually spent?

indicators.name: Change in domestic revenue
indicators.question: How did tax or domestic revenue collection change, in amount or as a share of GDP?

indicators.name: Stage reached by the public finance reform
indicators.question: How far did the targeted budget, tax or public finance law or reform get?

outcomes.statement: Budgets are credible and public money reaches priority services.

indicators.name: Change in budget credibility
indicators.question: How did the deviation between approved and actual budgets change over time?

indicators.name: Change in a budget or tax system score
indicators.question: How did an Open Budget Survey, TADAT or similar public finance score change?

indicators.name: Change in spending on priority services
indicators.question: How did public spending on priority services change as a result of better revenue or budget management?

categories.name: Regulation & regulatory quality
categories.definition: Changes in how rules for markets and public interests are designed, applied and enforced by regulators.
include: regulatory agencies and their independence
regulatory impact assessment
licensing, inspection and enforcement
simplification of administrative procedures
exclude: advocacy for a single rule, which belongs to advocacy & policy influence
sector results such as emissions or prices, which belong to the dimension of that sector
questions: How did the mandate, independence or capacity of a regulatory body change?
Which regulations were introduced, revised or repealed, and how were they assessed beforehand?
How is compliance with regulation inspected and enforced?
What change in the administrative burden on citizens or businesses is reported?

outcomes.statement: Regulators are set up or strengthened and proposed rules are assessed.

indicators.name: Regulatory staff trained
indicators.question: How many staff of regulatory or inspection bodies were trained?

indicators.name: Regulatory impact assessments carried out
indicators.question: How many regulatory impact assessments or regulatory reviews were carried out?

indicators.name: Regulatory body established
indicators.question: Was a regulatory body, unit or inspectorate established or given a new mandate?

outcomes.statement: Rules are revised, enforced and simpler to comply with.

indicators.name: Regulations revised
indicators.question: Which regulations were introduced, revised or repealed?

indicators.name: Inspections and enforcement actions
indicators.question: How many inspections, sanctions or enforcement actions were carried out, and with what result?

indicators.name: Change in the time or cost of procedures
indicators.question: How did the time or cost of a licence, permit or other administrative procedure change?

outcomes.statement: Regulated actors comply, regulation is predictable and regulators stay independent.

indicators.name: Change in compliance
indicators.question: How did the rate of compliance with the regulation change among regulated actors?

indicators.name: Change in a regulatory quality score
indicators.question: How did a regulatory quality score change (for example the WGI regulatory quality indicator or the OECD iREG indicators)?

indicators.name: Regulator independence secured
indicators.question: Are the regulator's independence and funding secured in law?

categories.name: Digital government & open data
categories.definition: Changes in the use of digital systems and data in public administration and public decision-making.
include: digital public services
digital identity and civil registration
open government data
data protection and public-sector AI rules
exclude: private-sector digital products
publication of fiscal or audit reports without a digital system, which belongs to governance & institutional capacity
questions: Which public services or administrative processes were digitised, and who uses them?
How did digital identity or civil registration coverage change?
What government data was opened, and how is it used?
Which rules on data protection, cybersecurity or the public use of AI were adopted?

outcomes.statement: Digital services and datasets are launched and officials can run them.

indicators.name: Digital public services launched
indicators.question: How many public services or administrative processes were digitised or launched online?

indicators.name: Government datasets published
indicators.question: How many government datasets were published as open data?

indicators.name: Officials trained in digital systems
indicators.question: How many public officials were trained to run or use the digital systems?

outcomes.statement: People use the digital services, identity coverage grows and data rules are adopted.

indicators.name: Uptake of digital services
indicators.question: How many people use the digital service, or what share of transactions is handled through it?

indicators.name: Identity or civil registration coverage
indicators.question: What share of the population holds a legal or digital identity or is recorded in the civil register?

indicators.name: Stage reached by data and digital rules
indicators.question: How far did the targeted law or policy on data protection, cybersecurity or public-sector AI get?

outcomes.statement: Public services are faster and cheaper, and digital government reaches everyone.

indicators.name: Change in service efficiency
indicators.question: How did the processing time, cost or error rate of public services change after digitisation?

indicators.name: Change in a digital government score
indicators.question: How did a digital government score change (for example the UN E-Government Development Index or the GovTech Maturity Index)?

indicators.name: Gap in use between groups
indicators.question: How does the use of digital public services differ between groups such as women, rural residents or older people?

categories.name: Media, information & public debate
categories.definition: Changes in the independence of the media, access to public information and the quality of public debate.
include: independent and public-interest journalism
access to information laws and requests
disinformation and information integrity
safety of journalists
exclude: an organisation's own communications or publicity
civil society space and freedom of association, which belong to civic participation & representation
questions: How did the independence, viability or reach of media outlets change?
What access to public information is provided by law, and how are requests handled?
How was disinformation or hate speech in public debate monitored or countered?
What is reported on threats to journalists or on their protection?

outcomes.statement: Journalists gain skills, reporting is produced and information requests are filed.

indicators.name: Journalists trained
indicators.question: How many journalists, editors or fact-checkers were trained or supported?

indicators.name: Reporting produced
indicators.question: Which investigations, broadcasts or fact-checks were produced, and how many?

indicators.name: Information requests filed
indicators.question: How many requests for public information were filed?

outcomes.statement: Authorities answer information requests and act on reporting, and information laws are adopted.

indicators.name: Information requests answered
indicators.question: What share of requests for public information was answered by the authorities?

indicators.name: Official action following reporting
indicators.question: Which official responses, investigations or policy changes followed media reporting?

indicators.name: Stage reached by the media or information law
indicators.question: How far did the targeted law on access to information, media or journalist protection get?

outcomes.statement: The media are free and safe, and the public has reliable information.

indicators.name: Change in a press freedom score
indicators.question: How did a press freedom score change (for example the RSF World Press Freedom Index or Freedom House)?

indicators.name: Change in the safety of journalists
indicators.question: How did attacks on, detentions of or legal harassment of journalists change?

indicators.name: Public trust in the media
indicators.question: How did public trust in the media or public exposure to reliable information change?

categories.name: Peace, security & conflict governance
categories.definition: Changes in political settlements, conflict prevention and the civilian governance of security institutions.
include: peace processes and agreements
dialogue, mediation and conflict prevention
security sector reform and civilian oversight
transitional justice and reconciliation mechanisms
exclude: humanitarian assistance, which belongs to humanitarian needs & response; civilian harm and attacks on protected objects in armed conflict, which belong to conduct of hostilities & IHL compliance
social cohesion between communities without a political or security process, which belongs to social cohesion & community
questions: What dialogue, mediation or peace process took place, and who took part?
Which agreements were reached, and how far have they been implemented?
How did civilian oversight, conduct or accountability of security forces change?
What change in political violence or conflict incidents is reported?

outcomes.statement: Conflict parties and communities enter dialogue and security personnel are trained.

indicators.name: Dialogues or mediation sessions held
indicators.question: How many dialogue, mediation or negotiation sessions were held?

indicators.name: Parties and groups taking part
indicators.question: Which parties, communities or groups, including women and young people, took part in dialogue or mediation?

indicators.name: Security personnel trained
indicators.question: How many police, military or other security personnel were trained, for example on human rights or accountability?

outcomes.statement: Agreements are reached and implemented, and security forces come under civilian oversight.

indicators.name: Agreements reached
indicators.question: Which ceasefires, peace agreements or local accords were reached?

indicators.name: Agreement provisions implemented
indicators.question: What share of the agreement's provisions was implemented?

indicators.name: Civilian oversight mechanism in use
indicators.question: Was a civilian oversight or complaints mechanism for security forces established and used?

outcomes.statement: Political violence falls, the settlement holds and people feel safe.

indicators.name: Change in violent incidents
indicators.question: How did the number of conflict incidents, deaths or cases of political violence change?

indicators.name: Settlement still holding
indicators.question: Is the peace agreement or political settlement still holding?

indicators.name: Perceived safety and trust in security forces
indicators.question: How did people's sense of safety or their trust in security forces change?

categories.name: International relations & cooperation
categories.definition: Changes in relations between states and in how governments take part in international and regional bodies and agreements.
include: diplomatic and multilateral engagement
regional integration and cross-border cooperation
negotiation of international agreements
development cooperation and aid coordination
exclude: compliance with treaty obligations and implementing legislation, which belong to legal frameworks & normative compliance
export values and trade policy, which belong to trade & export competitiveness; the current account, which belongs to macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
questions: Which international or regional processes did the government or organisation take part in, and with what positions?
What agreements, partnerships or joint commitments were negotiated or signed?
How is cross-border or regional cooperation organised and financed?
How is support from development partners coordinated with national priorities?

outcomes.statement: Governments and organisations take part in international processes with prepared positions.

indicators.name: Participation in international processes
indicators.question: Which international or regional conferences, negotiations or bodies did the actors take part in?

indicators.name: Delegates supported
indicators.question: How many delegates, negotiators or officials were trained or supported to take part?

indicators.name: Joint positions developed
indicators.question: Which common positions, declarations or proposals were prepared?

outcomes.statement: Agreements are signed and joint bodies are set up to carry them out.

indicators.name: Agreements or partnerships signed
indicators.question: Which international or regional agreements, memoranda or partnerships were signed?

indicators.name: Stage reached by the international commitment
indicators.question: How far did the targeted international agreement or commitment get?

indicators.name: Joint mechanism established
indicators.question: Was a joint body, secretariat or coordination mechanism established?

outcomes.statement: Commitments are delivered, cooperation is financed and external support follows national priorities.

indicators.name: International commitments delivered
indicators.question: How far were the international or regional commitments delivered in practice?

indicators.name: Financing mobilised through cooperation
indicators.question: What financing or other resources were mobilised through the cooperation?

indicators.name: External support aligned with national systems
indicators.question: What share of external support is aligned with, or channelled through, national plans, budgets or systems?

dimensions.name: Economy & finance
dimensions.definition: Changes in economic activity, incomes, employment, fiscal conditions, or access to finance and markets.

categories.name: Livelihoods, employment & income
categories.definition: Changes in jobs, earnings, job quality, or the security of household livelihoods and incomes.
include: job creation
wage, household income, consumption or income poverty change
informal or precarious work
employment, unemployment and labour force participation rates
exclude: macro-level GDP aggregates, which belong to macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
public budget allocations, which belong to public finance & budget management
employment services, wage subsidies and labour market rules, which belong to labour market policies & employment services

jobseeker training, apprenticeships and placement through employment programmes, which belong to labour market policies & employment services; enrolment and certification in formal technical and vocational institutions, which belong to technical & vocational education & adult literacy in the education dimension
the sales, profits and productivity of firms, which belong to enterprise growth & private investment
cash transfers, benefit payments and public works wages as programme outputs, which belong to social protection
questions: How many jobs were created by the project or programme, and how many of them went to women or young people?
What change in household income or workers' earnings is reported for participants or beneficiaries?
How did employment, unemployment or labour force participation rates change for women, young people or other groups?
How did the quality of jobs change, such as written contracts, social security coverage, regular pay or safe working conditions?

outcomes.statement: People receive livelihood support, take up short-term work and start income-generating activities.

indicators.name: People receiving livelihood support
indicators.question: How many people received livelihood support, such as productive assets, start-up grants, tools or business inputs?

indicators.name: Temporary work created
indicators.question: How many temporary or short-term jobs, or how many person-days of paid work, were created, for example in construction, maintenance or seasonal work, not public works programmes run as social protection?

indicators.name: Income-generating activities started
indicators.question: How many participants started a new income-generating activity or self-employment, such as a small trade, livestock rearing, crafts or a household business?

outcomes.statement: More people hold lasting jobs, and those jobs are more formal and better paid.

indicators.name: Lasting jobs created
indicators.question: How many permanent, full-time equivalent or formal jobs were created, not counting temporary work, internships or apprenticeship places, and for whom (for example women, youth or refugees)?

indicators.name: Change in participants' earnings
indicators.question: How did the wages or earnings of participating workers change, with before and after values or the difference from a comparison group?

indicators.name: Workers in formal employment
indicators.question: How many workers moved into formal employment, with a written contract or social security registration, as a count or a share?

outcomes.statement: Households have higher and more secure incomes, fewer live in poverty, and more people, including women and young people, are in work.

indicators.name: Change in household income
indicators.question: How did average household income, consumption or the income poverty rate change over several years, with before and after values?

indicators.name: Change in the unemployment rate
indicators.question: How did the unemployment rate or the employment rate change in the country, region or target group?

indicators.name: Change in labour force participation
indicators.question: How did the labour force participation rate change, for example for women or young people, with before and after rates?

categories.name: Macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
categories.definition: Changes in aggregate economic conditions such as growth, inflation, the fiscal balance, public debt and the external balance.
include: GDP growth
fiscal deficit, public debt and debt sustainability
inflation and monetary stance
current account, external debt and reserves
exclude: individual household income, which belongs to livelihoods, employment & income
single firm financial results, which belong to enterprise growth & private investment
budget preparation, tax administration and expenditure control, which belong to public finance & budget management
export performance and trade policy, which belong to trade & export competitiveness
contingency funds and disaster risk financing, which belong to disaster risk reduction & preparedness
tax revenue collected and tax administration performance, which belong to public finance & budget management
questions: What effect on the fiscal deficit, public debt or inflation is projected or observed from the policy reform or programme?
How is the sustainability of public debt assessed, and against which thresholds?
Which tax rate increases, exemption removals, subsidy cuts or wage bill measures were introduced to reduce the fiscal deficit?
By how much, as a share of GDP, are the fiscal deficit or public debt expected to fall as a result of the tax and spending measures?

outcomes.statement: Tax and spending measures are introduced, a fiscal rule is in force and the fiscal effect of the measures is estimated.

indicators.name: Fiscal policy measures adopted
indicators.question: Which tax rate changes, exemption removals, subsidy reforms or wage bill measures did the government introduce to change the deficit, with the amounts or rates?

indicators.name: Numerical fiscal rule in force
indicators.question: Is a numerical fiscal rule, such as a deficit, debt or expenditure ceiling, in force, and what limit does it set?

indicators.name: Expected fiscal yield of the measures
indicators.question: What saving or additional revenue are the fiscal measures expected to yield, in amount or as a share of GDP?

outcomes.statement: The fiscal balance improves, energy subsidy spending falls and inflation is contained.

indicators.name: Change in the fiscal balance
indicators.question: How did the overall or primary fiscal balance change as a share of GDP, with before and after values?

indicators.name: Change in energy subsidy spending
indicators.question: How did public spending on energy or fuel subsidies change, in amount or as a share of GDP?

indicators.name: Change in inflation
indicators.question: How did consumer price inflation change, with before and after rates?

outcomes.statement: Public debt is on a sustainable path and the economy grows steadily.

indicators.name: Change in public debt
indicators.question: How did public and publicly guaranteed debt change as a share of GDP, with before and after values?

indicators.name: Risk of debt distress
indicators.question: What overall risk rating, such as low, moderate, high or in debt distress, does the latest debt sustainability analysis assign?

indicators.name: Change in economic growth
indicators.question: How did real GDP growth or GDP per capita change, with before and after rates?

categories.name: Market access & financial inclusion
categories.definition: Changes in the ability of people or firms to reach markets, credit, insurance, or payment systems.
include: access to credit
accounts, savings, digital payments and remittance services
value chain or market linkage
insurance coverage
exclude: central bank monetary operations, which belong to macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
sovereign borrowing, which belongs to macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
finance for climate or environmental purposes, which belongs to climate & environmental finance
entry into export markets and trade policy, which belong to trade & export competitiveness
digital public services and identity systems, which belong to digital government & open data
health insurance and fee waivers, which belong to health systems & service delivery
questions: How did access to credit, savings, or insurance change for the target population?
Which credit guarantees, credit lines or microfinance products were provided to small enterprises, farmers or households?
How did ownership of bank or mobile money accounts change for women, rural people or the poor?
How many small producers or enterprises began selling to new domestic buyers, traders, cooperatives or processors?

outcomes.statement: Credit, financial education and links to buyers reach people, farmers and small enterprises.

indicators.name: Credit provided
indicators.question: How many loans, or how much credit, were provided to households, farmers or micro, small and medium enterprises, for example through a credit line, guarantee or microfinance institution?

indicators.name: People reached by financial education
indicators.question: How many people received financial education or financial literacy training?

indicators.name: Producers linked to buyers
indicators.question: How many producers or small enterprises were linked to buyers, traders, cooperatives, aggregators or contract farming schemes?

outcomes.statement: People and firms hold and use formal accounts, digital payments and insurance.

indicators.name: Adults with a financial account
indicators.question: How many adults have an account at a bank, microfinance institution or mobile money provider, as a count or a share of adults?

indicators.name: Use of digital payments
indicators.question: How did the use of digital payments change, for example salaries, transfers or taxes paid through accounts or mobile money, or the number of mobile money transactions, or the amount and cost of remittances received?

indicators.name: People covered by insurance
indicators.question: How many people, farmers or firms are covered by a commercial or micro-insurance product, such as crop, livestock, life or property cover (not health insurance or public schemes)?

outcomes.statement: Lending to small enterprises grows and stays sound, and small producers sell more through new markets.

indicators.name: Change in lending to small enterprises
indicators.question: How did lending to micro, small and medium enterprises change, in amount or as a share of total bank lending?

indicators.name: Change in loan portfolio quality
indicators.question: How did the quality of loans to households or small enterprises change, for example the non-performing loan ratio or portfolio at risk?

indicators.name: Change in sales through new market channels
indicators.question: How did the volume or value of products that producers or small enterprises sold through the new buyers, cooperatives or value chains change?

categories.name: Labour market policies & employment services
categories.definition: Changes in the programmes, services and rules that help jobseekers and workers find and keep work, such as employment services, job training for jobseekers, wage subsidies, labour law and managed labour migration.
include: public and private employment services, job counselling, job matching and job-search support
wage subsidies, hiring incentives, short job-training courses and apprenticeships for jobseekers and workers
labour law, employment contracts and minimum wages
managed labour migration and placement in jobs abroad
exclude: enrolment, curricula and certification in technical and vocational schools, colleges and institutes, which belong to technical & vocational education & adult literacy in the education dimension
jobs, earnings and employment rates in general, which belong to livelihoods, employment & income
public works payments and unemployment benefits, which belong to social protection
ratification of ILO conventions, which belongs to legal frameworks & normative compliance
the mandate and capacity of labour inspectorates as regulators, which belong to regulation & regulatory quality
questions: How many jobseekers found work through employment offices, job counselling, job matching or wage subsidies?
Which labour market rules changed, such as employment contract rules, dismissal protection or the minimum wage?
How many young people, women or long-term unemployed people took part in job-search support, short job-training courses, apprenticeships or wage subsidy schemes?
How many workers went to jobs abroad through managed labour migration or bilateral labour agreements?

outcomes.statement: Jobseekers are registered, counselled and trained, employers receive hiring incentives and labour rules are revised.

indicators.name: Jobseekers registered, counselled or trained
indicators.question: How many jobseekers or workers were registered, counselled or enrolled in a job-training course or apprenticeship by an employment programme?

indicators.name: Workers hired with a wage subsidy
indicators.question: How many workers were hired with a wage subsidy, social contribution waiver or other hiring incentive paid to employers?

indicators.name: Labour market rules changed
indicators.question: Which labour market rules were adopted or changed, for example employment contract types, dismissal rules, minimum wage or working-time rules?

outcomes.statement: Jobseekers are placed in jobs at home or abroad, and employers fill vacancies through the services.

indicators.name: Participants placed in jobs
indicators.question: How many participants of an employment service, job-training, apprenticeship or wage subsidy programme were in a job within a stated period afterwards, as a count or a share?

indicators.name: Vacancies filled through employment services
indicators.question: How many vacancies notified by employers were filled through the employment service or a job-matching platform?

indicators.name: Workers placed in jobs abroad
indicators.question: How many workers were placed in jobs abroad through a managed labour migration scheme or bilateral labour agreement?

outcomes.statement: Young people are in work or learning, employment is less segmented and employment programmes continue with public funding.

indicators.name: Change in youth not in employment, education or training
indicators.question: How did the share of young people not in employment, education or training (NEET) change?

indicators.name: Change in temporary employment
indicators.question: How did the share of employees on temporary or fixed-term contracts change, with before and after values?

indicators.name: Employment programme continued
indicators.question: Is the employment service, wage subsidy or labour migration programme continued by government with its own budget after the project?

categories.name: Enterprise growth & private investment
categories.definition: Changes in the creation, growth, productivity and innovation of private firms, and in the private investment they attract.
include: business development services, matching grants and advisory support to firms
new firm creation and entrepreneurship
firm sales, productivity and innovation, including state-owned enterprise performance, restructuring and privatisation
private and foreign direct investment
exclude: loans, guarantees and other access to finance for firms, which belong to market access & financial inclusion
business licensing, inspection and regulatory reform, which belong to regulation & regulatory quality
jobs and earnings of workers, which belong to livelihoods, employment & income
exports and entry into foreign markets, which belong to trade & export competitiveness
fiscal transfers to state-owned enterprises, which belong to macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
private finance mobilised for climate, energy or environmental purposes, which belongs to climate & environmental finance
the export sales of exporters and the yields of farms, which belong to trade & export competitiveness and to agricultural production & productivity
questions: How did the sales, profits or productivity of supported firms change?
Which business development services, matching grants or advisory support did small and medium enterprises receive?
How many new businesses were started or registered, including those owned by women or young people?
How much private or foreign direct investment, in dollars, was committed or attracted into businesses or sectors of the economy?

outcomes.statement: Firms receive business support and grants, and private investors commit capital.

indicators.name: Firms receiving business support
indicators.question: How many firms, entrepreneurs or micro, small and medium enterprises received business development services, business training, mentoring or advisory support?

indicators.name: Business grants awarded
indicators.question: How many matching grants or business grants were awarded to firms, and of what total value?

indicators.name: Private capital mobilised
indicators.question: How much private investment was committed or mobilised alongside the work, for example co-financing by firms, investor commitments or public-private partnership finance?

outcomes.statement: Supported firms adopt better practices and grow their sales, and new firms start.

indicators.name: New firms created
indicators.question: How many new firms or start-ups were started or formally registered as a result of the work?

indicators.name: Improved business practices adopted
indicators.question: Which improved management, production, quality or technology practices, or new products or processes, did supported firms adopt, for example bookkeeping, quality certification or new equipment?

indicators.name: Change in firm sales
indicators.question: How did the sales, turnover or revenue of supported firms change, with before and after values?

outcomes.statement: Firms are more productive and survive, and private investment in the economy grows.

indicators.name: Change in firm productivity
indicators.question: How did the productivity of supported firms or of a sector change, for example output or value added per worker, or total factor productivity?

indicators.name: Firm survival
indicators.question: How many supported or newly created firms were still operating two or more years later, as a count or a share?

indicators.name: Change in private investment
indicators.question: How did private investment or foreign direct investment inflows change, in amount or as a share of GDP?

categories.name: Trade & export competitiveness
categories.definition: Changes in exports, in firms' entry into foreign markets, and in the trade policies and standards that govern cross-border trade.
include: export values, volumes and diversification
firms and producers entering export markets
tariffs, non-tariff measures and trade agreements
product standards, quality certification and sanitary and phytosanitary compliance
exclude: logistics costs, transit times, ports and border clearance, which belong to freight & logistics
the current account and external balance, which belong to macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
customs revenue and tax administration, which belong to public finance & budget management
domestic buyers and value chains for small producers, which belong to market access & financial inclusion
the diplomatic negotiation of agreements and regional integration processes, which belong to international relations & cooperation
questions: How did the value, volume or diversity of exports change?
Which tariffs, non-tariff measures or trade agreements were changed, signed or implemented?
How many firms or producers started exporting or reached new foreign markets?
Which exporters or products obtained quality, food safety or sanitary and phytosanitary certification for foreign markets?

outcomes.statement: Exporters receive support, trade measures are adopted and quality infrastructure is put in place.

indicators.name: Exporters supported
indicators.question: How many firms, cooperatives or producers received export promotion, export readiness, trade fair or market intelligence support?

indicators.name: Trade policy measures adopted
indicators.question: Which trade policy measures were adopted, for example tariff reductions, removal of export bans, quotas or other non-tariff barriers, or a new trade agreement?

indicators.name: Quality infrastructure accredited
indicators.question: Was a testing laboratory, certification body or national standards body established, upgraded or internationally accredited?

outcomes.statement: Firms meet foreign standards, start exporting and sell more abroad.

indicators.name: Export certifications obtained
indicators.question: How many firms or producers obtained a certification required by foreign buyers, for example ISO, HACCP, GlobalG.A.P. or an SPS export certificate?

indicators.name: New exporters
indicators.question: How many firms or producers exported for the first time or entered a new export market?

indicators.name: Change in exports of supported firms
indicators.question: How did the export sales of supported firms or producers change, with before and after values?

outcomes.statement: The country's exports grow and diversify, and more of its firms export.

indicators.name: Change in national or sector exports
indicators.question: How did the value of the country's or the targeted sector's exports of goods and services change, with before and after values?

indicators.name: Change in export diversification
indicators.question: How did the diversity of exports change, for example the number of exported products or destination markets, or an export concentration index?

indicators.name: Change in the number of exporting firms
indicators.question: How did the number of exporting firms in the country or sector change, with before and after values?

categories.name: Agricultural production & productivity
categories.definition: Changes in crop, livestock and fisheries production and yields, and in farmers' use of improved inputs, technologies and farm services.
include: crop, livestock and fisheries production and yields
improved seeds, inputs, breeds, mechanisation and animal health
agricultural extension and advisory services
post-harvest losses, storage and processing
exclude: soil conservation, agroforestry and other sustainable land practices, which belong to sustainable land use, agriculture & forestry
irrigation water savings and water allocation, which belong to water resources management
farm incomes and rural jobs, which belong to livelihoods, employment & income
sales to buyers, contract farming and value chains, which belong to market access & financial inclusion
food security and nutrition, which belong to food security & nutrition
questions: How did crop yields, livestock production or fish catch change for participating farmers?
Which improved seeds, fertiliser, livestock breeds, farm equipment or extension advice did farmers receive?
How many smallholder farmers, women farmers or herders adopted improved seed varieties, breeds or farm equipment?
How did post-harvest losses of grain, produce or fish change after storage or processing improvements?

outcomes.statement: Farmers, herders and fishers receive improved inputs, advice and storage or processing facilities.

indicators.name: Farmers receiving extension services
indicators.question: How many farmers, herders or fishers received agricultural extension, advisory services or farmer field school training on production?

indicators.name: Improved farm inputs distributed
indicators.question: Which improved inputs were distributed, and in what quantity, for example certified seed, fertiliser, livestock, vaccines or fishing gear?

indicators.name: Storage and processing facilities built
indicators.question: How many storage, drying, cooling or processing facilities for crops, milk, meat or fish were built or rehabilitated?

outcomes.statement: Farmers adopt improved technologies, produce more per hectare or animal, and lose less after harvest.

indicators.name: Farmers adopting improved technology
indicators.question: How many farmers adopted an improved agricultural technology, such as improved seed varieties, fertiliser, mechanisation, improved breeds or animal health practices?

indicators.name: Change in yields
indicators.question: How did crop yields or livestock or fish productivity change, for example tonnes per hectare or litres of milk per animal, with before and after values?

indicators.name: Change in post-harvest losses
indicators.question: How did post-harvest losses change, as a quantity or as a share of the harvest?

outcomes.statement: Improved varieties and breeds spread, productivity per worker rises, and farm services continue without project support.

indicators.name: Change in area under improved production
indicators.question: How did the area planted with improved crop varieties, or the number of animals of improved breeds, change, with before and after values?

indicators.name: Change in agricultural productivity per worker or farm
indicators.question: How did agricultural value added per worker, or production per labour day, change, with before and after values?

indicators.name: Farm services sustained
indicators.question: Are extension, input supply or animal health services still provided after the project by government, cooperatives or private suppliers with their own funding?

categories.name: Digital connectivity & digital economy
categories.definition: Changes in the coverage, price and use of internet and mobile networks, and in the digital activity of people and firms.
include: broadband and mobile network infrastructure and coverage
telecommunications market reform and competition
internet and mobile broadband use and affordability
e-commerce, digital platforms and digital adoption by firms
exclude: digital public services, identity systems and open government data, which belong to digital government & open data
mobile money and digital payments, which belong to market access & financial inclusion
the independence and enforcement powers of the telecom regulator, which belong to regulation & regulatory quality
computers, internet connectivity and digital skills in schools, which belong to digital & remote learning in the education dimension
questions: How did mobile or broadband network coverage, or the number of internet subscriptions, change?
Which telecommunications sector reforms, such as awarding spectrum, licensing mobile or international gateway operators, or opening broadband and mobile markets to competition, were carried out?
What share of women, rural residents or low-income households use the internet or own a mobile phone, and how did it change?
How many businesses started selling online or using digital tools, such as e-commerce platforms or digital accounting?

outcomes.statement: Networks are extended, telecommunications markets are opened and firms receive support to go digital.

indicators.name: Telecommunications infrastructure built
indicators.question: How much telecommunications infrastructure was built or upgraded, for example kilometres of fibre-optic cable, mobile towers, a submarine cable landing or an internet exchange point?

indicators.name: Telecommunications market reforms adopted
indicators.question: Which telecommunications market reforms were adopted, for example new operator licences, spectrum allocation, infrastructure sharing rules or opening the international gateway?

indicators.name: Firms supported to adopt digital tools
indicators.question: How many firms or entrepreneurs received support to adopt digital tools or to sell online?

outcomes.statement: More people are covered by networks and subscribe to broadband, and more firms use digital tools.

indicators.name: Population covered by mobile broadband
indicators.question: How many people are covered by a 3G, 4G or 5G mobile network or a fixed broadband network, as a count or a share of the population?

indicators.name: Change in broadband subscriptions
indicators.question: How did the number of mobile broadband or fixed broadband subscriptions change, in total or per 100 people?

indicators.name: Firms adopting digital tools
indicators.question: How many firms started selling online or using digital tools such as e-commerce platforms, digital accounting or online marketing?

outcomes.statement: Internet access is affordable and widely used, and gaps in use between groups narrow.

indicators.name: People using the internet
indicators.question: How many people use the internet, as a count or a share of the population?

indicators.name: Change in the price of internet access
indicators.question: How did the price of mobile data or fixed broadband change, for example the cost of 1 GB as a share of monthly income per person?

indicators.name: Change in the internet use gap
indicators.question: How did the gap in internet use between women and men, or between rural and urban people, change, with before and after values?

dimensions.name: Social impact
dimensions.definition: Changes in wellbeing, equity, social relations, and access to essential services.

categories.name: Health & wellbeing
categories.definition: Changes in physical or mental health, illness, mortality, or subjective wellbeing.
include: mortality, including maternal, child and premature deaths
incidence and prevalence of disease, injury and disability
mental health and psychosocial wellbeing
health behaviours and subjective wellbeing
exclude: nutritional status and food security, which belong to food security & nutrition
the coverage, quality and cost of health services, which belong to health systems & service delivery
health sector budget lines without a health outcome, which belong to health systems & service delivery
occupational safety compliance paperwork
road traffic deaths and injuries, which belong to road safety
the delivery of emergency health care and outbreak response, which belongs to health systems & service delivery or to humanitarian needs & response
questions: What change in health status, mortality, or morbidity is reported?
How did mental health, psychological distress or life satisfaction change among the people reached?
Which health outcome measures, such as mortality rates, disease incidence or DALYs, are used to assess the effect?
What evidence shows that a health programme changed illness, death or wellbeing, for example from a trial, a before-and-after survey or a comparison group?

outcomes.statement: People are reached with health promotion, disease prevention and psychosocial support.

indicators.name: People reached by health promotion
indicators.question: How many people were reached by health education or disease prevention activities, such as awareness sessions, peer education or home visits, on topics other than water, sanitation and hygiene?

indicators.name: Preventive health items distributed
indicators.question: How many preventive health items were distributed, such as insecticide-treated bed nets, condoms or self-test kits?

indicators.name: People receiving psychosocial support
indicators.question: How many people received counselling, psychosocial support or mental health care for stress, depression or trauma, other than as survivors of violence?

outcomes.statement: People adopt healthier behaviours, and illness and psychological distress fall.

indicators.name: Change in a health risk behaviour
indicators.question: How did a health risk behaviour change, such as tobacco or alcohol use, physical inactivity, unsafe sex or sleeping without a bed net?

indicators.name: Change in disease incidence or prevalence
indicators.question: How did the incidence or prevalence of a disease or condition change, for example malaria, tuberculosis, HIV, diarrhoea or hypertension?

indicators.name: Change in mental health
indicators.question: How did a measure of mental health or psychological distress change, for example depression or anxiety scores such as the PHQ-9, GAD-7 or K10?

outcomes.statement: Fewer people die early and people live healthier and more satisfied lives.

indicators.name: Change in a mortality rate
indicators.question: How did a mortality rate change, for example maternal, under-five, infant or neonatal mortality, or deaths from a specific disease?

indicators.name: Change in disability or years lived in good health
indicators.question: How did the prevalence of disability or chronic illness, or life expectancy or healthy life expectancy, change?

indicators.name: Change in subjective wellbeing
indicators.question: How did life satisfaction, quality of life or subjective wellbeing change, for example measured with the WHO-5, EQ-5D or a life satisfaction scale?

categories.name: Health systems & service delivery
categories.definition: Changes in the availability, coverage, quality and affordability of health services, and in the workforce, facilities and financing that deliver them.
include: coverage and use of essential health services such as immunisation, antenatal care and skilled birth attendance
health workforce, facilities, medicines and supplies
quality of care and patient experience
health insurance, user fees and financial protection from health costs
exclude: the illness, mortality or wellbeing results of care, which belong to health & wellbeing
nutrition programmes and nutritional status, which belong to food security & nutrition
water, sanitation and hygiene in health facilities, which belong to water, sanitation & hygiene
commercial insurance, savings and credit products, which belong to market access & financial inclusion
general public budget processes, which belong to public finance & budget management
questions: How did the coverage or use of health services change, for example immunisation, antenatal care, facility births or outpatient visits?
Which health facilities, health workers, medicines or equipment were added or improved?
What barriers to health care, such as distance, user fees, waiting times or out-of-pocket costs, do patients report?
What findings are reported on the quality of health care, such as adherence to clinical guidelines or patient satisfaction?

outcomes.statement: Health facilities, health workers, medicines and equipment become available to serve the population.

indicators.name: Health facilities built or upgraded
indicators.question: How many health facilities, such as clinics, health posts, health centres or hospitals, were built, rehabilitated or equipped?

indicators.name: Health workers trained or deployed
indicators.question: How many health workers, such as doctors, nurses, midwives or community health workers, were trained or deployed, other than for nutrition work?

indicators.name: Medicines and equipment supplied
indicators.question: Which medicines, vaccines, medical equipment or supplies were provided to health facilities?

outcomes.statement: More people use essential health services and the quality of care improves.

indicators.name: Change in coverage of an essential health service
indicators.question: How did the coverage of an essential health service change, for example full immunisation or DTP3, four or more antenatal visits, skilled birth attendance or HIV treatment?

indicators.name: Health service visits
indicators.question: How many outpatient visits, consultations, admissions or patients treated were recorded at the health facilities?

indicators.name: Change in quality of care
indicators.question: How did a measure of the quality of care change, for example adherence to clinical guidelines, waiting times, stock-outs of essential medicines or patient satisfaction?

outcomes.statement: People obtain the health care they need without financial hardship.

indicators.name: Population covered by health insurance or free care
indicators.question: How many of the target population are enrolled in a health insurance scheme or entitled to free care, as a count or a share?

indicators.name: Change in out-of-pocket health spending
indicators.question: How did out-of-pocket health spending, or the share of households facing catastrophic health expenditure (SDG 3.8.2), change?

indicators.name: Change in unmet need for health care
indicators.question: How did the share of people who report unmet need for health care, or who went without care because of cost, distance or waiting times, change?

categories.name: Food security & nutrition
categories.definition: Changes in people's access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food, and in their nutritional status.
include: household food security, hunger and food consumption
diet quality, dietary diversity and the affordability of a healthy diet
stunting, wasting, underweight and micronutrient deficiencies
nutrition programmes such as supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplements and infant feeding counselling
exclude: crop yields and farm production, which belong to agricultural production & productivity; farm incomes, which belong to livelihoods, employment & income
emergency food, cash and nutrition assistance as deliveries, which belong to humanitarian needs & response (the resulting acute malnutrition and food insecurity stay here)
the effect of school meals on enrolment, which belongs to the education dimension
diet-related illness such as diabetes, which belongs to health & wellbeing
questions: How did household food security or hunger change, for example months of food shortage or meals eaten per day?
What change in child stunting, wasting, underweight or anaemia is reported?
Which nutrition interventions were delivered, such as supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplements or infant feeding counselling?
Which food security or nutrition measures are used, such as the FIES, dietary diversity scores, months of adequate household food provisioning or height-for-age z-scores?

outcomes.statement: Children, women and caregivers receive nutrition services, and children's growth is monitored.

indicators.name: People receiving nutrition services
indicators.question: How many children, pregnant or breastfeeding women or other people received supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplements or nutrition counselling?

indicators.name: Children in growth monitoring
indicators.question: How many children under five were weighed and measured in growth monitoring and promotion sessions or nutrition screening?

indicators.name: Nutrition workers trained
indicators.question: How many health workers, community nutrition volunteers or lead mothers were trained in nutrition or infant and young child feeding?

outcomes.statement: Households eat more and better food, and infant feeding practices improve.

indicators.name: Change in household food consumption
indicators.question: How did household food consumption change, for example calorie intake, the number of meals eaten per day or months of adequate household food provisioning (MAHFP)?

indicators.name: Change in dietary diversity
indicators.question: How did dietary diversity change, for example the minimum dietary diversity for women (MDD-W), for children aged 6 to 23 months, or a household dietary diversity score?

indicators.name: Infants exclusively breastfed
indicators.question: How many infants under six months were exclusively breastfed, as a count or a share?

outcomes.statement: Undernutrition falls and people are food secure throughout the year.

indicators.name: Change in child stunting
indicators.question: How did the prevalence of stunting (low height-for-age) among children, or their height-for-age z-scores, change?

indicators.name: Change in wasting, underweight or anaemia
indicators.question: How did the prevalence of wasting, underweight or anaemia change among children or women, including acute malnutrition (GAM or SAM) in a crisis?

indicators.name: Change in the prevalence of food insecurity
indicators.question: How did the prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity or of undernourishment change, for example measured with the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (SDG 2.1.2) or the prevalence of undernourishment (SDG 2.1.1)?

categories.name: Equity & inclusion
categories.definition: Changes in the distribution of benefits and outcomes across groups, and in the inclusion of, or discrimination against, marginalised groups.
include: gaps in outcomes between income, location, ethnic, age or disability groups
disability inclusion and accessibility
inclusion of marginalised groups such as indigenous peoples, minorities and migrants
discrimination and stigma
exclude: formal legal rights without evidence of practice, which belong to legal frameworks & normative compliance
generic diversity statements
women's agency and gender norms, which belong to gender equality & women's empowerment; gender-based violence, which belongs to gender-based violence & child protection
trust and relations between communities, which belong to social cohesion & community
the representation of groups in public decision-making, which belongs to civic participation & representation

human rights violations against at-risk groups and their protection, which belong to protection & human rights; the rights of refugees and displaced people, which belong to forced displacement & durable solutions
gaps in enrolment and learning between groups of learners, which belong to equity & inclusion in education
questions: How did programme benefits or service use differ between income groups, ethnic groups, disability status or urban and rural areas?
What change in the gap between rich and poor, urban and rural, or ethnic or disability groups is reported for a health, education, income or service outcome?
What was done to include persons with disabilities, minorities or other marginalised groups, such as accessibility measures or targeted outreach?
What is reported on discrimination, stigma or social exclusion experienced by persons with disabilities, minorities, migrants or people living with HIV?

outcomes.statement: Marginalised groups are reached and barriers to their participation are removed.

indicators.name: People from marginalised groups reached
indicators.question: How many people from marginalised groups were reached, such as persons with disabilities, ethnic minorities, indigenous peoples, migrants or the poorest households?

indicators.name: Accessibility measures provided
indicators.question: Which accessibility measures or reasonable accommodations were provided, such as ramps, assistive devices like wheelchairs, sign language interpretation or materials in minority languages?

indicators.name: Target for reaching marginalised groups
indicators.question: Was a target or quota set for reaching marginalised groups, such as a minimum share of beneficiaries who are persons with disabilities or from the poorest quintile, and was it met?

outcomes.statement: Marginalised groups use services and opportunities on a more equal footing.

indicators.name: Change in the gap in service use between groups
indicators.question: How did the gap in access to or use of a service between groups change, for example between the poorest and richest quintile, rural and urban areas, or people with and without disabilities?

indicators.name: Inclusion policies adopted or applied
indicators.question: Which inclusion or anti-discrimination policies, accessibility standards or rules for targeting marginalised groups were adopted or applied by service providers?

indicators.name: Change in barriers faced by marginalised groups
indicators.question: How did the barriers that marginalised groups report, such as cost, distance, language, stigma or inaccessible buildings, change?

outcomes.statement: Disparities between groups narrow and marginalised people face less discrimination.

indicators.name: Change in an outcome gap between groups
indicators.question: How did the gap in an outcome such as health, income or schooling between groups change, measured as a ratio or a difference between quintiles, regions, ethnic groups or disability status?

indicators.name: Change in a summary inequality measure
indicators.question: How did a summary inequality measure change, for example the Gini coefficient, the concentration index, the slope index of inequality or the income share of the bottom 40% (SDG 10.1.1)?

indicators.name: Change in reported discrimination
indicators.question: How did the share of people who report discrimination or stigma, for example because of disability, ethnicity, migration status or HIV status, change?

categories.name: Gender equality & women's empowerment
categories.definition: Changes in the agency, decision-making and rights of women and girls, and in the gender roles, norms and laws that shape them.
include: women's decision-making and control over household income and assets
gender roles, norms and discriminatory attitudes in the household and community
unpaid care work, time use and women's freedom of movement
discriminatory laws and customary rules on inheritance, land, marriage and work
exclude: women in elected office and public decision-making, which belong to civic participation & representation
women's jobs, earnings and access to credit, which belong to the economic dimension
girls' enrolment and learning, which belong to the education dimension
gender-based violence, services for survivors, child protection and child marriage, which belong to gender-based violence & child protection
the split of programme beneficiaries by sex alone, which belongs to equity & inclusion
questions: How did women's participation in household decisions or their control over income and assets change?
