indicators.question: How did the use of public transport, or its accessibility and safety, change for women, people with disabilities, older people or low-income passengers?

categories.name: Walking, cycling & active travel
categories.definition: Changes in the conditions for, and the amount of, walking, cycling and other non-motorised travel.
include: footpaths, crossings and pedestrian areas
cycle lanes, bicycle parking and bike sharing
levels of walking and cycling
street design and traffic calming for non-motorised users
exclude: deaths and injuries of pedestrians and cyclists, which belong to road safety
mode share and modal shift across all transport modes, which belong to mobility & transport access
parks, squares and recreational space, which belong to land use & urban planning or, within settlement upgrading, to housing & informal settlements
health effects of physical activity, which belong to health & wellbeing
questions: How did the number of people walking or cycling, or the number of trips on foot or by bicycle, change?
What footpaths, pedestrian crossings, cycle lanes or bike-sharing schemes were built or introduced?
How safe and comfortable are footpaths, crossings and cycle lanes for people walking or cycling, including children and people with disabilities?
What walking or cycling plan, policy, street design standard or budget was adopted?

outcomes.statement: Footpaths, cycle lanes and bike-sharing schemes are built, and plans for walking and cycling are adopted.

indicators.name: Footpaths and cycle lanes built
indicators.question: How many kilometres of footpaths, sidewalks, cycle lanes or cycle tracks were built or improved?

indicators.name: Bike sharing and bicycle parking provided
indicators.question: What bike-sharing scheme or bicycle parking was introduced, for example the number of shared bicycles, docking stations or parking spaces?

indicators.name: Walking and cycling plan adopted
indicators.question: Was a walking, cycling or non-motorised transport plan, policy or street design standard adopted?

outcomes.statement: People use the new walking and cycling facilities, find them safe and comfortable, and street space is given to them.

indicators.name: Use of walking and cycling facilities
indicators.question: How many pedestrians or cyclists use the new footpaths, cycle lanes or bike-sharing scheme, for example counts per day or bike-share trips?

indicators.name: Rating by pedestrians and cyclists
indicators.question: How do pedestrians or cyclists rate the safety, comfort or accessibility of the streets, for example in a user survey or walkability audit?

indicators.name: Street space given to walking and cycling
indicators.question: Was street or road space reallocated to walking and cycling, for example car lanes converted, streets pedestrianised or speed limits lowered?

outcomes.statement: Walking and cycling are common, connected and possible for everyone across the city.

indicators.name: Change in city-wide walking and cycling
indicators.question: How did walking and cycling across the city change, for example the share of residents who cycle regularly or of children who walk or cycle to school?

indicators.name: Coverage of the walking and cycling network
indicators.question: How much of the city's streets has footpaths or belongs to a connected cycle network, as a length or a share?

indicators.name: Accessibility of streets for all users
indicators.question: How did the accessibility of streets and crossings change for people with disabilities, older people or children, for example ramps, tactile paving or safe crossings?

categories.name: Freight & logistics
categories.definition: Changes in how goods are moved, handled and cleared, and in the cost, time and reliability of freight transport.
include: freight volumes and the split between road, rail and water
logistics costs and transit times
ports, freight terminals, logistics centres and border crossings
performance and finances of railway, port and freight operators
exclude: export values and trade policy, which belong to trade & export competitiveness; the current account, which belongs to macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
market linkages and value chains for producers, which belong to market access & financial inclusion
passenger travel, which belongs to mobility & transport access and to public transport services & operations
general tax and customs administration reform, which belongs to public finance & budget management
questions: How did freight volumes, tonnage or the share of goods moved by rail, road or water change?
What change in the transit time, cost or clearance time of freight transport is reported for the corridor, port or border?
Which freight terminals, logistics centres or port and rail freight connections were built or upgraded?
How did the efficiency or finances of the railway, port or freight operator change, for example locomotive availability, operating cost per tonne-kilometre or the operating ratio?

outcomes.statement: Freight facilities and rolling stock are added and logistics strategies are prepared.

indicators.name: Freight facilities built or upgraded
indicators.question: Which freight terminals, logistics centres, port facilities, rail sidings or border posts were built or upgraded?

indicators.name: Freight capacity added
indicators.question: How much freight capacity was added, for example locomotives, wagons, trucks or terminal throughput capacity?

indicators.name: Freight or logistics strategy prepared
indicators.question: Was a freight, logistics or trade facilitation strategy, study or technical standard completed?

outcomes.statement: More goods move through the improved services, more of them by the targeted mode, and they move faster.

indicators.name: Change in freight volume
indicators.question: How did the volume of freight handled change, for example tonnes, tonne-kilometres or containers (TEU), with before and after values?

indicators.name: Share of freight on the targeted mode
indicators.question: What share of freight tonnage moves by rail, inland waterway or another targeted mode, as a share or a tonnage?

indicators.name: Change in freight transit and clearance time
indicators.question: How did freight transit time, dwell time at a port or terminal, or border clearance time change?

outcomes.statement: Moving goods is cheaper and more reliable, and logistics performance improves.

indicators.name: Change in freight and logistics cost
indicators.question: How did the cost of moving freight change, for example the cost per tonne-kilometre, per container or as a share of the value of goods?

indicators.name: Change in freight operator efficiency
indicators.question: How did the operating efficiency of the railway, port or freight operator change, for example operating cost per tonne-kilometre, locomotive or equipment availability, or the operating ratio?

indicators.name: Change in freight reliability
indicators.question: How did the reliability of freight deliveries change, for example on-time arrival, delays, loss and damage of goods, or a corridor performance score?

categories.name: Housing & informal settlements
categories.definition: Changes in the supply, affordability, quality and security of housing, and in the upgrading of slums, informal settlements and their neighbourhood facilities.
include: housing supply and affordability
social, rental and subsidised housing and housing finance
slum and informal settlement upgrading, including public spaces, street lighting and community facilities
security of tenure and housing quality
exclude: zoning and land use rules that enable housing, which belong to land use & urban planning

household water and sanitation services outside a housing or upgrading programme, which belong to water, sanitation & hygiene; household energy services outside such a programme, which belong to access to basic services
emergency shelter for people in crisis, which belongs to humanitarian needs & response
replacement housing for people displaced by a project, which belongs to land acquisition, displacement & resettlement
schools and health facilities as services, which belong to school access & participation and to health systems & service delivery
questions: How did housing supply, house prices, rents or housing affordability change in the area studied?
How many homes were built, repaired or financed through social housing, subsidies or housing loans?
What upgrading took place in slums or informal settlements, such as roads, drainage, street lighting, public spaces, markets or secure tenure?
Which households lack adequate housing, for example because of overcrowding, insecure tenure or poor construction?

outcomes.statement: Homes are built or improved, settlements are upgraded and households receive housing finance.

indicators.name: Housing units built or rehabilitated
indicators.question: How many housing units were built, completed or rehabilitated?

indicators.name: People in upgraded settlements
indicators.question: How many people live in the slums or informal settlements that were upgraded with roads, drainage, street lighting, public spaces or other improvements?

indicators.name: Housing finance provided
indicators.question: What housing subsidies, mortgages, housing microloans or rental support were provided, and to how many households?

outcomes.statement: Households hold secure tenure, upgraded neighbourhood assets are maintained and housing policies are adopted.

indicators.name: Households with secured tenure
indicators.question: How many households received a title, lease, occupancy certificate or other document that secures their tenure?

indicators.name: Upkeep of upgraded neighbourhood assets arranged
indicators.question: Is there an arrangement and a budget for operating and maintaining the roads, drainage, street lighting and public spaces of the upgraded settlement, for example with the municipality or a community group?

indicators.name: Stage reached by the housing policy
indicators.question: How far did the targeted housing or slum upgrading policy, law or national programme get?

outcomes.statement: Fewer people live in slums or inadequate housing, upgraded neighbourhoods are better places to live, and housing is affordable.

indicators.name: Population living in slums or inadequate housing
indicators.question: How did the number or share of people living in slums, informal settlements or inadequate housing change, with before and after values (for example SDG indicator 11.1.1)?

indicators.name: Change in housing affordability
indicators.question: How did housing affordability change, for example the share of income spent on housing, the house price to income ratio or rent levels?

indicators.name: Change in living conditions in upgraded settlements
indicators.question: How did living conditions in the upgraded settlements change, for example flooding, safety, access to services or resident satisfaction in a survey?

categories.name: Land acquisition, displacement & resettlement
categories.definition: Changes for people who lose land, homes or livelihoods to infrastructure and urban development, and in how they are compensated and resettled.
include: land acquisition and involuntary resettlement
compensation and livelihood restoration
evictions and displacement caused by redevelopment
grievance redress for affected people
exclude: displacement by conflict or disaster, which belongs to forced displacement & durable solutions and to humanitarian needs & response
rising rents and housing affordability in redeveloped areas, which belong to housing & informal settlements
noise, dust and other environmental effects of construction, which belong to the environmental dimension
environmental and social assessment procedures in general, such as impact assessments and management plans, which belong to environmental assessment, safeguards & compliance
questions: How many people or households were displaced or lost land or assets because of the project or redevelopment?
What compensation, replacement housing or resettlement assistance was provided to affected people?
How did the incomes, livelihoods or living standards of resettled or affected people change afterwards?
How were complaints and grievances about land acquisition, eviction or resettlement handled?

outcomes.statement: Affected people are identified, a resettlement plan is in place and compensation is paid.

indicators.name: People affected by land acquisition
indicators.question: How many people are affected by land acquisition, displacement or the loss of assets? Give people; if the document counts only households, give the households and say so.

indicators.name: Resettlement plan prepared
indicators.question: Was a resettlement action plan, resettlement policy framework or livelihood restoration plan prepared?

indicators.name: Affected people compensated
indicators.question: How many of the affected people or households received their compensation, as a count or a share?

outcomes.statement: Households are relocated, grievances are resolved and affected people take up livelihood support.

indicators.name: Households relocated
indicators.question: How many households were physically relocated to new housing or a resettlement site because of a project or redevelopment?

indicators.name: Grievances resolved
indicators.question: How many of the complaints or grievances about land acquisition or resettlement were resolved, as a count or a share?

indicators.name: Livelihood restoration support taken up
indicators.question: What livelihood restoration support, such as training, jobs, replacement land or business grants, did affected people take up?

outcomes.statement: Resettled people regain or improve their incomes and living conditions.

indicators.name: Change in incomes of affected people
indicators.question: How do the incomes or livelihoods of resettled or affected people compare with before their displacement?

indicators.name: Change in living conditions of resettled people
indicators.question: How do the housing, tenure security or access to services of resettled people compare with before their relocation?

indicators.name: Satisfaction of affected people
indicators.question: How satisfied are resettled or affected people with their compensation or resettlement site, for example in a survey or completion audit?

dimensions.name: Humanitarian concerns, law & rights
dimensions.definition: Changes in protection of people in crisis, in human rights, and in compliance with legal and normative frameworks.

categories.name: Protection & human rights
categories.definition: Changes in the safety, dignity and rights of people, particularly those exposed to violence, abuse, exploitation, arbitrary detention or discrimination.
include: protection monitoring and the documentation of human rights violations
freedom from killing, torture, enforced disappearance and arbitrary detention
statelessness, persecution and discriminatory restrictions imposed on minorities and other at-risk groups
remedy, redress and reparation obtained by victims
exclude: refugees, internally displaced people and durable solutions, which belong to forced displacement & durable solutions
the protection of children, sexual and gender-based violence and trafficking in persons, which belong to gender-based violence & child protection
civilian harm from military operations, which belongs to conduct of hostilities & IHL compliance
the capacity and performance of courts and legal aid services, which belong to rule of law & justice institutions
freedom of expression, association and the press, which belong to civic participation & representation and to media, information & public debate
questions: How did the number of documented human rights violations, such as killings, torture, disappearances or arbitrary detention, change?
Which protection activities, such as protection monitoring, community protection committees or individual protection assistance, were carried out?
Which rights are denied or at risk, and for which groups, such as minorities, detainees, human rights defenders, stateless people or people with disabilities?
Did victims of human rights violations obtain remedy, such as compensation, restitution, rehabilitation or reparations?

outcomes.statement: Violations are monitored, people at risk receive protection assistance and protection mechanisms are set up.

indicators.name: Protection or human rights monitoring carried out
indicators.question: Was protection or human rights monitoring carried out, for example through monitoring visits, incident reporting or visits to places of detention?

indicators.name: People at risk receiving protection assistance
indicators.question: How many people at risk received protection assistance, such as individual protection assistance, protection counselling or referral to specialised services?

indicators.name: Protection mechanisms set up
indicators.question: Which protection mechanisms, such as community protection committees, protection monitoring networks or human rights complaint desks, were set up?

outcomes.statement: Authorities act on documented violations, unlawful detention ends and victims obtain remedy.

indicators.name: Documented violations followed up by authorities
indicators.question: Of the human rights violations documented, how many were followed up by the authorities, for example through an investigation, a release or a corrective measure, as a count or a share? If the document gives no count, answer unknown.

indicators.name: People released from arbitrary detention
indicators.question: How many people held in arbitrary or unlawful detention were released, or had their detention reviewed by an independent body?

indicators.name: Victims obtaining remedy
indicators.question: How many victims of human rights violations received compensation, restitution, rehabilitation or reparations?

outcomes.statement: Violations fall and groups that were at risk can exercise their rights safely.

indicators.name: Change in human rights violations
indicators.question: How did killings, torture, enforced disappearances or arbitrary detention change over time?

indicators.name: Change in a human rights score
indicators.question: How did a human rights or physical integrity score change (for example the CIRIGHTS index, the Political Terror Scale or the Human Rights Measurement Initiative scores)?

indicators.name: Rights now exercised by an excluded minority or stateless group
indicators.question: Which rights, such as nationality, civil documentation or equal access to public services, can a previously excluded minority or stateless group now exercise? Do not count refugees or displaced people.

categories.name: Humanitarian needs & response
categories.definition: Assessment of needs arising from crisis, and the reach, quality, and accountability of assistance provided.
include: needs assessment
assistance coverage and reach
accountability to affected populations
timeliness and modality of assistance, including food, cash, water, shelter and relief items
exclude: long-term development programming, which belongs to the dimension of its result
malnutrition, food insecurity, disease and mortality as outcomes, which belong to food security & nutrition and to health & wellbeing in the social dimension
access constraints, coordination and localisation, which belong to humanitarian access, coordination & localisation
early warning, contingency planning and pre-arranged disaster risk financing, which belong to disaster risk reduction & preparedness
legal doctrine, which belongs to legal frameworks & normative compliance
questions: What humanitarian needs were assessed, and how severe are they judged to be?
How many affected people were reached with assistance, and with what gap remaining?
How quickly did humanitarian assistance reach affected people after the crisis began?
What feedback from affected populations is reported, and how was it acted on?

outcomes.statement: Needs are assessed and affected people receive assistance and relief items.

indicators.name: Needs assessment carried out
indicators.question: Was a needs assessment of the crisis-affected population carried out, for example a multi-sector initial rapid assessment (MIRA), a household survey or a multi-sector needs assessment?

indicators.name: People reached with humanitarian assistance
indicators.question: How many crisis-affected people received humanitarian assistance of any kind, such as food, cash, shelter, water or relief items?

indicators.name: Shelter and relief items distributed
indicators.question: How many emergency shelter materials or non-food items, such as tents, tarpaulins, blankets or hygiene kits, were distributed?

outcomes.statement: Assistance covers the people in need, arrives in time and is adjusted to what affected people say.

indicators.name: Coverage of people in need
indicators.question: Of the people assessed as in need, how many were reached with assistance, as a count or a share?

indicators.name: Time taken for assistance to arrive
indicators.question: How many days or weeks after the onset of the crisis did assistance reach affected people?

indicators.name: Changes made in response to feedback
indicators.question: What changes did agencies make to the assistance in response to complaints or feedback from affected people?

outcomes.statement: Humanitarian needs fall, affected people judge the assistance fair and relevant, and the response hands over to longer-term systems.

indicators.name: Change in unmet humanitarian needs
indicators.question: How did the number of people in need or the severity of their needs change, for example in a JIAF severity score or a humanitarian needs overview?

indicators.name: Affected people's view of the assistance
indicators.question: How did affected people rate the relevance, fairness or sufficiency of the assistance they received, for example in perception or post-distribution surveys?

indicators.name: Handover to national or development programmes
indicators.question: How far was the humanitarian response handed over to national services, social protection or development programmes?

categories.name: Legal frameworks & normative compliance
categories.definition: Changes in law, treaty obligation, or normative standards, and in the degree to which actors comply with them.
include: analysis of what treaties, customary rules and national laws require
treaty ratification and national implementing legislation
reporting to and recommendations of treaty bodies, the Universal Periodic Review and special procedures
compliance with rulings of international and regional human rights courts, commissions and treaty bodies
exclude: operational programme delivery, which belongs to humanitarian needs & response
advocacy for a law without a legal instrument tabled or adopted, which belongs to advocacy & policy influence
the independence, capacity and case handling of domestic courts, which belong to rule of law & justice institutions
how parties to an armed conflict conduct military operations, which belongs to conduct of hostilities & IHL compliance
questions: Which provisions of a human rights, refugee or humanitarian law treaty, customary rule or national statute govern the situation, and what do they require of the state or of armed groups?
Which gaps or differences between national law or practice and an international human rights, refugee or humanitarian law obligation are identified?
Which recommendations of treaty bodies, the Universal Periodic Review or special rapporteurs did the state accept or implement?
Did the state carry out the measures ordered in a ruling of an international or regional human rights court, commission or treaty body that found a violation?

outcomes.statement: The state takes on international obligations, reviews its law against them and reports to the monitoring bodies.

indicators.name: Treaties ratified or acceded to
indicators.question: Which international or regional treaties, protocols or conventions did the state ratify or accede to, such as the Refugee Convention, the CRPD or the Additional Protocols to the Geneva Conventions?

indicators.name: Review of national law against the obligation
indicators.question: Was national law reviewed against the requirements of a treaty or standard, for example in a legal gap analysis or a compatibility study?

indicators.name: Reports submitted to monitoring bodies
indicators.question: How many periodic reports did the state submit to UN treaty bodies, the Universal Periodic Review or regional human rights bodies?

outcomes.statement: Implementing laws are adopted and the state acts on the recommendations and rulings of monitoring bodies.

indicators.name: Stage reached by the implementing law
indicators.question: How far did the national law that gives effect to the treaty or standard get?

indicators.name: Human rights recommendations implemented
indicators.question: Of the recommendations from treaty bodies, the Universal Periodic Review or special procedures, how many did the state implement, as a count or a share?

indicators.name: Rulings of human rights bodies carried out
indicators.question: Did the state carry out the measures ordered by a human rights court, commission or UN treaty committee, such as the European Court of Human Rights, the Inter-American Court or the Human Rights Committee?

outcomes.statement: Obligations are applied in practice and independent bodies find the state compliant.

indicators.name: Change in assessed compliance
indicators.question: How did the state's compliance with the obligation in practice change, as assessed by a treaty body, special rapporteur or independent monitor?

indicators.name: Obligation applied by national authorities
indicators.question: How do national courts, ministries or administrative bodies apply the treaty or implementing law in their decisions?

indicators.name: Obligations found unmet in practice
indicators.question: Which obligations under a treaty or national law does a treaty body, court, special rapporteur or the document's own analysis find are not met in practice?

categories.name: Forced displacement & durable solutions
categories.definition: Changes in the protection, legal status and rights of refugees, asylum seekers and internally displaced people, and in their progress towards durable solutions.
include: asylum, refugee status determination and protection from refoulement
registration, documentation, detention and freedom of movement of displaced people
refugees' and displaced people's rights to work, housing, health care and education in practice
durable solutions: voluntary return, local integration and resettlement
exclude: displacement caused by infrastructure or urban development, which belongs to land acquisition, displacement & resettlement
accession to refugee treaties and the drafting of national refugee law, which belong to legal frameworks & normative compliance
relief delivered in camps and settlements, which belongs to humanitarian needs & response
the incomes, learning and health outcomes of displaced people, which belong to the economic, education and social dimensions
questions: How did the number of refugees, asylum seekers or internally displaced people change?
What legal status, documentation or protection from refoulement did refugees and asylum seekers receive?
Which rights, such as the right to work, to move freely or to use public health care and schools, can refugees or displaced people exercise in the host country?
How many refugees or internally displaced people returned, integrated locally or were resettled?

outcomes.statement: Displaced people are registered and documented, asylum claims are decided and solutions are planned.

indicators.name: Displaced people registered or documented
indicators.question: How many refugees, asylum seekers or internally displaced people were registered or received identity or civil documents?

indicators.name: Asylum claims decided
indicators.question: How many asylum or refugee status applications were decided?

indicators.name: Durable solutions plan prepared
indicators.question: Was a plan for durable solutions prepared, for example a national IDP policy, a pledge under the Global Compact on Refugees or a solutions strategy?

outcomes.statement: Refugees are recognised, are not returned to danger and can use their rights in the host country.

indicators.name: Refugee recognition rate
indicators.question: Of the asylum applications decided, how many were granted refugee status or complementary protection, as a count or a share?

indicators.name: Rights gained by displaced people in practice
indicators.question: Which rights did refugees or internally displaced people gain in practice, such as a work permit, freedom of movement, release from immigration detention or access to national health care and schools?

indicators.name: Refoulement and pushbacks reported
indicators.question: What cases of refoulement, pushbacks, forced returns or denial of access to asylum were reported?

outcomes.statement: Displaced people reach durable solutions and live on equal terms with their hosts.

indicators.name: Displaced people reaching a durable solution
indicators.question: How many refugees or internally displaced people returned voluntarily, were resettled to a third country or integrated locally, for example through naturalisation?

indicators.name: Change in protracted displacement
indicators.question: How did the number of people in protracted displacement, or the length of time people stay displaced, change?

indicators.name: Gap between displaced people and their hosts
indicators.question: How do displaced people compare with the host population in safety, housing, documentation or income, for example against the IASC criteria for durable solutions?

categories.name: Gender-based violence & child protection
categories.definition: Changes in the protection of children from violence, exploitation, recruitment, child marriage and family separation, and in the prevention of and response to sexual and gender-based violence, including in armed conflict, displacement and other crises.
include: child protection case management, family tracing and reunification
child labour, adult and child trafficking, and the recruitment and use of children by armed forces and groups
sexual and gender-based violence, including intimate partner violence, conflict-related sexual violence and child marriage
services for survivors, such as clinical management of rape, psychosocial support, hotlines, shelters and safe spaces
exclude: gender norms, attitudes and women's decision-making without violence, which belong to gender equality & women's empowerment
the prosecution of violence cases by courts, which belongs to rule of law & justice institutions
bullying and violence at school, which belong to school infrastructure & learning environment
children's school enrolment and learning, which belong to the education dimension
questions: How did reported cases of sexual or gender-based violence, such as intimate partner violence, conflict-related sexual violence or child marriage, change?
Which services, such as clinical management of rape, psychosocial support, hotlines, shelters or women and girls safe spaces, were available to survivors of sexual and gender-based violence?
How many unaccompanied, separated or other children at risk received case management or were reunified with their families?
How did child labour, trafficking in persons or the recruitment of children by armed forces or armed groups change?

outcomes.statement: Survivors of violence and children at risk receive services, and safe spaces and shelters open.

indicators.name: Children at risk receiving case management
indicators.question: How many children at risk, such as unaccompanied, separated or formerly associated children, received case management or alternative care?

indicators.name: Safe spaces and shelters set up
indicators.question: How many child-friendly spaces, women and girls safe spaces, shelters or one-stop centres for survivors of violence were set up?

indicators.name: Survivors of gender-based violence receiving services
indicators.question: How many survivors of sexual or gender-based violence received medical care, psychosocial support, shelter or safety services?

outcomes.statement: Separated children return to their families, survivors get care in time and acceptance of violence falls.

indicators.name: Separated children reunified
indicators.question: How many unaccompanied or separated children were reunified with their families or placed in family-based care?

indicators.name: Change in acceptance of violence against women and children
indicators.question: How did the share of women or men who think violence against a wife or partner, or harsh physical punishment of children, is justified change, for example in a DHS attitudes module or a social norms survey?

indicators.name: Survivors receiving care within 72 hours
indicators.question: Of the survivors of sexual violence who reached a health facility, how many received care within 72 hours of the incident, as a count or a share? If the document gives no count, answer unknown.

outcomes.statement: Sexual and gender-based violence falls and fewer children are married early, recruited, trafficked or exploited.

indicators.name: Change in sexual and gender-based violence
indicators.question: How did sexual or gender-based violence change, for example intimate partner violence prevalence (DHS or SDG 5.2.1), UN-verified cases of conflict-related sexual violence or GBVIMS data?

indicators.name: Change in grave violations against children
indicators.question: How did the recruitment and use of children, abduction of children or sexual violence against children in armed conflict change (for example in UN-verified grave violations cases)?

indicators.name: Change in child marriage, child labour and trafficking
indicators.question: How did child marriage, child labour, trafficking in persons or the sexual exploitation of children change (for example SDG 5.3.1, 8.7.1 or 16.2.2)?

categories.name: Conduct of hostilities & IHL compliance
categories.definition: Changes in how parties to armed conflict respect international humanitarian law, in the harm their operations cause to civilians and protected objects, and in accountability for violations.
include: civilian harm from attacks, explosive weapons and landmines
protection of hospitals, schools, cultural property and other protected objects
treatment of detainees, the wounded and the missing in armed conflict
integration of IHL into military doctrine and weapons reviews, and investigation of alleged violations
exclude: peace processes, security sector reform and transitional justice mechanisms, which belong to peace, security & conflict governance
ratification of IHL treaties and national implementing laws, which belong to legal frameworks & normative compliance
torture, detention and other violations outside the conduct of armed conflict, which belong to protection & human rights
attacks on aid workers and access for humanitarian organisations, which belong to humanitarian access, coordination & localisation
questions: How did civilian deaths and injuries caused by attacks, shelling, air strikes or explosive weapons change?

What commitments, rules or policies, such as military manuals, rules of engagement, Deeds of Commitment or codes of conduct, did armed forces or armed groups adopt to comply with international humanitarian law?
Which protected persons or objects, such as hospitals, health workers, schools or detainees, were attacked or harmed in the armed conflict?
Which war crimes or other serious violations of international humanitarian law were investigated or prosecuted, and with what result?

outcomes.statement: Armed actors commit to IHL and violations and civilian harm start being recorded.

indicators.name: Commitments by armed actors to respect IHL
indicators.question: How many armed forces or armed groups signed commitments to respect international humanitarian law, such as Geneva Call Deeds of Commitment, codes of conduct or unilateral declarations?

indicators.name: Civilian harm tracking set up
indicators.question: Was a civilian harm tracking or casualty recording mechanism set up, for example by armed forces, a UN mission or an independent monitoring group?

indicators.name: Alleged IHL violations recorded
indicators.question: How many alleged violations of international humanitarian law, such as indiscriminate attacks or attacks on hospitals or schools, were recorded by monitors or commissions of inquiry?

outcomes.statement: Armed actors change their military practice, give access to detainees and investigate alleged violations.

indicators.name: Military practice revised to integrate IHL
indicators.question: Which military manuals, rules of engagement, targeting procedures or weapons reviews were revised to integrate international humanitarian law?

indicators.name: Independent access to detainees
indicators.question: Did a party to the armed conflict give the ICRC or another independent body access to the people it detained?

indicators.name: Alleged IHL violations investigated
indicators.question: How many alleged violations of international humanitarian law were investigated by the responsible party, a commission of inquiry or a court, as a count or a share of those recorded? If the document gives no count, answer unknown.

outcomes.statement: Civilian harm and attacks on protected objects fall and violations are punished.

indicators.name: Change in civilian casualties from hostilities
indicators.question: How did the number of civilians killed or injured by attacks, shelling, air strikes, explosive weapons or landmines change, for example in UN-verified casualty counts or monitor data such as Airwars? Do not count combatant deaths or overall conflict incidents.

indicators.name: Change in attacks on protected objects
indicators.question: How did attacks on hospitals, health workers, schools or other protected objects change (for example in the WHO Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care)?

indicators.name: Convictions or sanctions for IHL violations
indicators.question: Which war crimes or other serious violations of international humanitarian law led to a conviction by a national, military or international court, or to a disciplinary sanction? Do not count truth commissions, amnesties or reconciliation processes.

categories.name: Humanitarian access, coordination & localisation
categories.definition: Changes in the ability of humanitarian organisations to reach people in need, in how responders coordinate, and in the role and funding of local and national actors.
include: humanitarian access constraints and principled access negotiations
safety and security of humanitarian workers
coordination through clusters, joint response plans and pooled funds
localisation: the funding, leadership and capacity of local and national responders
exclude: the number of people reached and the assistance they received, which belong to humanitarian needs & response
development cooperation and aid effectiveness, which belong to international relations & cooperation
attacks on civilians and protected objects other than aid workers, which belong to conduct of hostilities & IHL compliance
questions: What restrictions on humanitarian access, such as denied movement, bureaucratic impediments or insecurity, prevented aid from reaching people?
How many aid workers were killed, injured, kidnapped or attacked?
What funding, partnerships or leadership roles did local and national humanitarian organisations receive?
How did coordination among humanitarian organisations, for example through clusters or a joint response plan, change?

outcomes.statement: Access is negotiated, coordination bodies start working and local organisations are supported.

indicators.name: Access arrangements agreed
indicators.question: Were access arrangements agreed with authorities or armed groups, such as humanitarian corridors, pauses, cross-line or cross-border deliveries or deconfliction?

indicators.name: Coordination mechanism set up
indicators.question: Was a humanitarian coordination mechanism set up, such as a cluster, a sector working group or a humanitarian country team?

indicators.name: Local organisations supported
indicators.question: How many local or national organisations received capacity strengthening, training or partnership agreements from international agencies?

outcomes.statement: Funding reaches the response and local actors, and local organisations take up leadership roles.

indicators.name: Share of funding to local and national actors
indicators.question: How much humanitarian funding went as directly as possible to local and national organisations, as an amount or a share of the total?

indicators.name: Share of the appeal funded
indicators.question: What share of the requirements of the humanitarian response plan or appeal was funded?

indicators.name: Local organisations in leadership roles
indicators.question: Which coordination or decision-making roles, such as cluster co-lead or a seat on a pooled fund board, do local or national organisations now hold?

outcomes.statement: Aid reaches people in need more safely and the response is better coordinated and more locally led.

indicators.name: Change in humanitarian access
indicators.question: How did humanitarian access to people in need change, for example in the number of access incidents or the population living in hard-to-reach areas?

indicators.name: Change in attacks on aid workers
indicators.question: How did the number of aid workers killed, injured or kidnapped change (for example in the Aid Worker Security Database)?

indicators.name: Change in the effectiveness of coordination
indicators.question: How did the effectiveness of humanitarian coordination change, for example less duplication, fewer gaps in coverage or joint needs analysis?

dimensions.name: Education
dimensions.definition: Changes in access to education, in learning, and in the capacity of education systems.

categories.name: School access & participation
categories.definition: Changes in enrolment, attendance, retention, progression and completion in primary and secondary education.
include: enrolment and attendance
dropout and retention
completion and transition rates
barriers to schooling
exclude: measured learning achievement, which belongs to learning outcomes & quality
teacher workforce policy, which belongs to teachers & school leadership
preschool enrolment, which belongs to early childhood education & school readiness; university enrolment, which belongs to higher education & research
gaps in participation between girls and boys or other groups of learners, which belong to equity & inclusion in education
questions: What change in enrolment, attendance, or completion is reported, and for which cohort?
What was done to bring out-of-school children into school or to stop students from dropping out?
What barriers keep children and adolescents out of school, such as fees, distance, work or early marriage?
How are school enrolment, attendance or dropout measured, for example as gross or net enrolment, average daily attendance or chronic absenteeism?

outcomes.statement: Barriers to schooling are reduced and out-of-school children are brought into school.

indicators.name: Students receiving support to attend school
indicators.question: How many students received support to enrol in or stay in school, such as scholarships, fee waivers, school-attendance cash transfers, uniforms or school transport?

indicators.name: Out-of-school children enrolled
indicators.question: How many out-of-school children or dropouts were enrolled or re-enrolled in school, including through catch-up or accelerated learning programmes?

indicators.name: Attendance and dropout prevention measures
indicators.question: Which measures to raise attendance or prevent dropout were put in place, for example early warning systems, attendance monitoring, mentoring or outreach to families?

outcomes.statement: More children enrol and attend school regularly, and fewer repeat grades or drop out.

indicators.name: Change in school enrolment
indicators.question: How did enrolment in primary or secondary school change, as a number of students or as a gross or net enrolment rate?

indicators.name: Change in student attendance
indicators.question: How did student attendance change, for example the attendance rate, average daily attendance or the share of chronically absent students?

indicators.name: Change in dropout or grade repetition
indicators.question: How did the dropout, grade repetition or retention rate of the students or schools concerned change?

outcomes.statement: More young people complete primary and secondary school and leave with more years of schooling.

indicators.name: Change in completion or graduation rate
indicators.question: How did the primary, lower secondary or upper secondary completion rate, or the high school graduation rate, change?

indicators.name: Change in transition to the next school level
indicators.question: How did the number or share of students moving on to the next level of schooling change, for example from primary to lower secondary school?

indicators.name: Change in educational attainment of young people
indicators.question: How did the share of young people with at least lower secondary education, or their average years of schooling, change?

categories.name: Learning outcomes & quality
categories.definition: Changes in what learners know and can do, and in the curricula and learning materials meant to improve it.
include: assessment and test results
literacy and numeracy
curriculum, textbooks and learning materials
learning gain measurement
exclude: enrolment counts, which belong to school access & participation
school construction, which belongs to school infrastructure & learning environment
teacher training and classroom teaching practice, which belong to teachers & school leadership
learning gaps between groups of learners, which belong to equity & inclusion in education
questions: What change in learning achievement is measured, and with which assessment?
How large is the reported gain in student test scores, for example in standard deviations or scale-score points?
Which curriculum, textbook or reading and mathematics programme was introduced to improve student learning?
What share of students reach grade-level or minimum proficiency in reading or mathematics?

outcomes.statement: Learners receive improved curricula, learning materials and structured reading, mathematics or remedial programmes.

indicators.name: Textbooks and learning materials distributed
indicators.question: How many textbooks, reading books or other teaching and learning materials were distributed to schools or students?

indicators.name: Curriculum or learning standards revised
indicators.question: Was a curriculum, syllabus or set of learning standards revised or newly introduced?

indicators.name: Students reached by learning programmes
indicators.question: How many students took part in a structured reading, mathematics, tutoring or remedial learning programme?

outcomes.statement: Participating students' scores and pass rates improve and fewer students remain at the lowest performance level.

indicators.name: Change in participants' assessment scores
indicators.question: How did the participating students' scores on a reading, mathematics or other learning assessment change, for example on EGRA, EGMA, a state test or a school exam?

indicators.name: Change in examination pass rates
indicators.question: How did pass rates in national, school-leaving or end-of-cycle examinations change, as a count or a share of candidates?

indicators.name: Change in students at the lowest performance level
indicators.question: How did the share of students at the lowest performance level, for example 'below basic' on a state test or NAEP, change?

outcomes.statement: More learners reach minimum proficiency in literacy and numeracy, and gains last beyond the programme.

indicators.name: Students reaching minimum proficiency
indicators.question: How many students, as a count or a share, reach the minimum or grade-level proficiency standard in reading or mathematics, for example 'proficient' on a state test or NAEP, or level 2 in PISA?

indicators.name: Persistence of learning gains
indicators.question: What did follow-up assessments one or more years after the programme ended show about the size of the learning gain compared with the end of the programme?

indicators.name: Trend in large-scale assessment results
indicators.question: How did results in a national or international large-scale assessment change over several years, for example NAEP, PISA, TIMSS, PIRLS or a national learning assessment?

categories.name: Teachers & school leadership
categories.definition: Changes in the supply, qualification, practice and retention of teachers, and in the leadership of schools.
include: teacher recruitment, deployment and retention
teacher qualifications and professional development
classroom teaching practice and teacher evaluation
head teacher and principal leadership
exclude: student learning results, which belong to learning outcomes & quality
student enrolment, which belongs to school access & participation
education planning, financing and data systems, which belong to education governance, financing & management
civil service reform across government, which belongs to governance & institutional capacity in the political dimension

training of preschool educators, technical and vocational instructors and university lecturers, which belongs to early childhood education & school readiness, to technical & vocational education & adult literacy and to higher education & research
questions: What change in teacher supply, qualification, or retention is reported?
How was teacher effectiveness or classroom practice measured, for example through classroom observation, student surveys or evaluation ratings?
What training, induction, coaching or mentoring was provided to school teachers or principals?
Which schools or areas lack qualified teachers, for example rural, high-poverty or hard-to-staff schools?

outcomes.statement: Teachers and school leaders are recruited, trained and supported.

indicators.name: Teachers trained
indicators.question: How many primary or secondary school teachers received pre-service or in-service training, coaching or mentoring?

indicators.name: Teachers recruited or deployed
indicators.question: How many new primary or secondary school teachers were recruited, hired or deployed to schools?

indicators.name: Head teachers or principals trained
indicators.question: How many head teachers, principals or other school leaders were trained in school leadership or management?

outcomes.statement: Teachers apply new practices in the classroom, and more teachers are qualified and present.

indicators.name: Change in observed classroom practice
indicators.question: How did teachers' classroom practice change, as observed or rated with a tool such as Teach, a classroom observation protocol or a lesson observation checklist?

indicators.name: Qualified or certified teachers
indicators.question: How many teachers, as a count or a share, have the required minimum qualification or certification, for example 'highly qualified' teachers or teachers trained to national standards?

indicators.name: Change in teacher absence
indicators.question: How did teacher absence from school or from the classroom change?

outcomes.statement: A stable, qualified teaching workforce is fairly distributed across schools.

indicators.name: Change in teacher attrition or retention
indicators.question: How did the number or share of teachers leaving the profession or their school change?

indicators.name: Change in pupil-teacher ratio
indicators.question: How did the number of pupils per teacher, or per trained or qualified teacher, change?

indicators.name: Stage of teacher policy reform
indicators.question: How far did a reform of teacher standards, certification, career paths, deployment rules or pay get?

categories.name: Early childhood education & school readiness
categories.definition: Changes in young children's participation in early childhood education and in their readiness for primary school.
include: preschool, kindergarten and pre-primary enrolment
early childhood educators and programme quality
school readiness and early development
transition from preschool to primary school
exclude: child health, nutrition and growth, which belong to health & wellbeing and to food security & nutrition in the social dimension
childcare provided so that parents can work, and its effect on parents' jobs, which belong to livelihoods, employment & income in the economic dimension
primary school enrolment, which belongs to school access & participation
questions: How did enrolment in preschool, kindergarten or pre-primary education change?
Which early childhood education centres, classrooms or programmes were opened or expanded?
Which young children gained access to early learning, for example children from low-income or rural families?
How was children's school readiness or early development measured, for example with IDELA, the ECDI or a kindergarten readiness assessment?

outcomes.statement: Early learning places, programmes and trained educators are put in place and children enrol.

indicators.name: Early learning centres or classrooms established
indicators.question: How many preschool, kindergarten or early childhood education centres or classrooms were established or upgraded?

indicators.name: Early childhood educators trained
indicators.question: How many preschool teachers, caregivers or other early childhood educators were trained?

indicators.name: Children enrolled in early learning programmes
indicators.question: How many children were enrolled in the supported preschool, kindergarten, Head Start or other early learning programmes?

outcomes.statement: More young children attend early learning of good quality, especially in the year before primary school.

indicators.name: Change in pre-primary participation rate
indicators.question: How did the pre-primary enrolment rate, or the share of children in organised learning one year before primary school, change?

indicators.name: Quality rating of early learning settings
indicators.question: How did the quality of early learning settings change, as rated with a tool such as ECERS, CLASS, MELQO or a national quality rating system?

indicators.name: Early learning curriculum or standards adopted
indicators.question: Was an early learning curriculum, early learning standards or a quality framework for pre-primary education adopted?

outcomes.statement: Children start primary school ready to learn and their early gains carry into later grades.

indicators.name: Children developmentally on track or ready for school
indicators.question: How many children, as a count or a share, are developmentally on track or assessed as ready for school, for example on IDELA, the ECDI or a kindergarten readiness assessment?

indicators.name: Later school results of early learning participants
indicators.question: How did children who attended early learning do later in school, for example in early grade reading, grade repetition or special education placement?

indicators.name: Progress towards universal pre-primary education
indicators.question: How far did the commitment to free or universal preschool or pre-primary education get?

categories.name: Technical & vocational education & adult literacy
categories.definition: Changes in participation in, and the quality and recognition of, formal technical and vocational education, and in adult literacy and non-formal education.
include: technical and vocational schools, colleges, institutes and skills training centres
competency-based TVET curricula, instructors and apprenticeships leading to a recognised qualification
adult literacy and non-formal education
qualification frameworks and certification of TVET learners
exclude: programmes run by employment services for jobseekers, such as job counselling, job matching and wage subsidies, and the job placements that follow, which belong to labour market policies & employment services in the economic dimension
jobs and earnings after training, which belong to livelihoods, employment & income in the economic dimension
university and college degrees, which belong to higher education & research
questions: How did enrolment in, or completion of, technical and vocational schools, colleges or institutes change?
Which technical and vocational institutions, programmes or curricula were set up, upgraded or revised?
What change in reading, writing or numeracy is reported for participants of adult literacy or non-formal education programmes?
How were the skills of technical and vocational students assessed or certified, for example through competency assessments, trade tests or national qualifications?

outcomes.statement: Technical and vocational institutions are equipped and their courses updated, and youth and adults join literacy programmes.

indicators.name: TVET institutions built or upgraded
indicators.question: How many technical and vocational schools, colleges, institutes or training centres were built, upgraded or equipped?

indicators.name: Learners in adult literacy or non-formal education
indicators.question: How many adults or out-of-school youth enrolled in literacy, numeracy, adult basic education or other non-formal learning programmes?

indicators.name: Competency-based TVET curricula developed
indicators.question: Which competency-based curricula, occupational standards or TVET programmes were developed or revised, for example with employer input?

outcomes.statement: More students enrol in and complete technical and vocational education with recognised qualifications, and adult learners complete their courses.

indicators.name: Change in TVET enrolment
indicators.question: How did enrolment in technical and vocational schools, colleges or institutes change, as a number of students or a share of upper secondary or post-secondary students?

indicators.name: TVET students completing and certified
indicators.question: How many students of technical and vocational schools, colleges or institutes completed their programme, as a count or a share? If a pass rate on a certification, trade test or competency assessment is given instead, say so.

indicators.name: Adult learners completing literacy courses
indicators.question: How many adult learners, as a count or a share, completed a literacy or non-formal education course or passed its assessment?

outcomes.statement: More youth and adults are literate, adult learners keep their literacy gains, and vocational qualifications are recognised nationally.

indicators.name: Change in youth or adult literacy rate
indicators.question: How did the literacy rate of youth or adults change, in the programme area or nationally?

indicators.name: Stage of the qualifications framework
indicators.question: How far did a national qualifications framework or system for recognising skills and prior learning get?

indicators.name: Literacy gains of adult learners
indicators.question: What change in reading, writing or numeracy scores or skill levels was reported for adult learners who completed a literacy or non-formal education programme?

categories.name: Higher education & research
categories.definition: Changes in access to, quality of and completion of tertiary education, and in the research capacity of universities.
include: university and college enrolment and completion
quality assurance and accreditation
tertiary scholarships and student financial aid
research output and postgraduate training
exclude: graduate employment and earnings, which belong to livelihoods, employment & income in the economic dimension
short vocational courses and apprenticeships, which belong to technical & vocational education & adult literacy
research and innovation by firms, which belongs to enterprise growth & private investment in the economic dimension
questions: How did enrolment in, or graduation from, universities and colleges change?
Which higher education programmes or institutions were accredited, reviewed or newly established?
Which students received scholarships, grants or loans for university or college study?
How did university research output change, for example peer-reviewed publications, PhD graduates or research grants won?

outcomes.statement: Students and academic staff receive support, and degree programmes are set up or improved.

indicators.name: Tertiary scholarships or grants awarded
indicators.question: How many scholarships, grants or student loans for university or college study were awarded?

indicators.name: Degree programmes accredited or introduced
indicators.question: How many degree programmes were accredited, re-accredited or newly introduced?

indicators.name: Academic staff trained or upgraded
indicators.question: How many lecturers or other academic staff received training or completed a master's or PhD? Give separate numbers if reported.

outcomes.statement: More students enrol in and complete tertiary education, and quality assurance is applied.

indicators.name: Change in tertiary enrolment
indicators.question: How did the number of students, or the gross enrolment ratio, in universities, colleges or other tertiary institutions change?

indicators.name: Change in tertiary completion or persistence
indicators.question: How did graduation, completion or persistence rates of university or college students change?

indicators.name: External quality assurance in operation
indicators.question: Is an external quality assurance or accreditation agency or process regularly reviewing higher education institutions or programmes?

outcomes.statement: Universities produce more research of recognised quality, and tertiary education becomes more affordable and open to low-income students.

indicators.name: Change in research output
indicators.question: How did the number of peer-reviewed publications, PhD graduates, citations or competitive research grants of the supported institutions change?

indicators.name: Change in tertiary affordability and equity
indicators.question: How did tuition fees, student debt or the share of low-income students in universities and colleges change, for example after a tuition-free or free-college policy?

indicators.name: Accreditation status of the institution
indicators.question: What accreditation status did the supported university or college reach?

categories.name: Equity & inclusion in education
categories.definition: Changes in the gaps in access and learning between groups of learners, and in the inclusion of girls, learners with disabilities, minorities and other disadvantaged learners.
include: gender parity in education
inclusive education for learners with disabilities or special educational needs
learners from minority-language, ethnic, refugee or low-income groups
targeted support and funding for disadvantaged learners
exclude: social inclusion and discrimination outside education, which belong to equity & inclusion in the social dimension
protection of children from violence, exploitation or recruitment, which belongs to gender-based violence & child protection in the humanitarian concerns, law & rights dimension
overall enrolment that is not broken down by group, which belongs to school access & participation
questions: How did the gap in school enrolment or completion between girls and boys, or between other groups of learners, change?
What support was provided to include learners with disabilities or special educational needs in school?
Which groups of learners remain behind, such as girls, minority-language speakers, refugees, low-income or rural students?
What funding, policy or law supports the schooling of girls, learners with disabilities or minority-language learners?

outcomes.statement: Disadvantaged learners are identified and receive support suited to their needs.

indicators.name: Learners receiving inclusion support
indicators.question: How many learners with disabilities, minority-language or refugee learners received inclusion support, such as assistive devices, specialist teaching assistants, accessible materials or mother-tongue instruction?

indicators.name: Learners screened for disabilities or special needs
indicators.question: How many children were screened for, or identified as having, a disability or special educational need?

indicators.name: Measures to make schools inclusive
indicators.question: Which measures were taken to make schools more inclusive of girls, minority or disadvantaged learners, for example gender-responsive teaching, recruiting female teachers, bilingual instruction or anti-discrimination rules?

outcomes.statement: Inclusion policies and needs-based funding are applied and more disadvantaged learners attend mainstream schools.

indicators.name: Learners with disabilities in school
indicators.question: How did the number or share of learners with disabilities enrolled in school, or taught in regular classrooms, change?

indicators.name: Stage of the inclusive education policy
indicators.question: How far did a policy or law on inclusive education, special educational needs or gender equality in education get?

indicators.name: Needs-based funding for disadvantaged learners
indicators.question: Is extra funding allocated to schools or students according to disadvantage, for example a weighted funding formula, Title I funds or needs-based grants?

outcomes.statement: Gaps in participation, completion and learning between groups of learners narrow.

indicators.name: Change in gender parity in education
indicators.question: How did the gender parity index, or the ratio of girls to boys, in enrolment, completion or learning change?

indicators.name: Change in the achievement gap between groups
indicators.question: How did the gap in test scores or proficiency between groups of students, for example by income, race or ethnicity, language or disability, change?

indicators.name: Change in completion for disadvantaged learners
indicators.question: How did completion or graduation rates of disadvantaged groups, such as the poorest households, rural students or learners with disabilities, change?

categories.name: School infrastructure & learning environment
categories.definition: Changes in the condition, facilities, basic services and safety of schools and other learning spaces.
include: classroom construction and rehabilitation
water, sanitation, hygiene and electricity in schools
accessible and disaster-resilient school buildings
bullying, violence and safety at school
exclude: roads, housing and other infrastructure outside schools, which belong to infrastructure condition & investment and to housing & informal settlements in the urban structures & transport dimension

drinking water and sanitation services for households, communities, health facilities and markets, which belong to water, sanitation & hygiene; school feeding and school health services, which belong to food security & nutrition and to health systems & service delivery in the social dimension
attacks on schools, which belong to conduct of hostilities & IHL compliance; education as part of a humanitarian response, which belongs to humanitarian needs & response
early warning and disaster preparedness outside school buildings, which belong to disaster risk reduction & preparedness in the environmental dimension
computers and internet connectivity for learning, which belong to digital & remote learning
questions: How did the condition of school buildings and classrooms change, for example overcrowding or classrooms in poor repair?
How many classrooms or schools were built, rehabilitated or extended?
Which schools gained drinking water, toilets, handwashing facilities or electricity?
What change in bullying, violence or students' sense of safety at school is reported?

outcomes.statement: Classrooms and school facilities are built, repaired and made safer.

indicators.name: Classrooms built or rehabilitated
indicators.question: How many classrooms were built, rehabilitated or extended?

indicators.name: Schools given water and sanitation facilities
indicators.question: How many schools received new or repaired drinking water points, toilets or latrines, or handwashing facilities?

indicators.name: School safety measures introduced
indicators.question: Which school safety measures were introduced, for example anti-bullying programmes, codes of conduct, safe routes to school or school safety plans?

outcomes.statement: Students learn in less crowded schools with working basic services that are kept in use.

indicators.name: Change in pupils per classroom
indicators.question: How did the number of pupils per classroom, or the share of overcrowded classrooms or schools running double shifts, change?

indicators.name: Schools with basic water, sanitation and electricity
indicators.question: How many schools, as a count or a share, have basic drinking water, basic sanitation or electricity? Give the figure for the service reported and name it.

indicators.name: School facilities maintained and in use
indicators.question: Are the built or repaired classrooms and facilities in use and maintained, for example through a maintenance budget or a school committee?

outcomes.statement: Schools provide a safe, healthy, accessible and resilient learning environment.

indicators.name: Change in bullying or violence at school
indicators.question: How did the share of students experiencing bullying, corporal punishment or violence at school, or the number of reported incidents, change?

indicators.name: Schools meeting safety or accessibility standards
indicators.question: How many schools, as a count or a share, meet building safety, disaster-resilience or disability-accessibility standards?

indicators.name: Change in the condition of school buildings
indicators.question: How did the share of schools or classrooms rated in good condition change, for example in a school facilities survey or condition assessment?

categories.name: Digital & remote learning
categories.definition: Changes in learners' and teachers' access to and use of digital technology and remote learning, including to keep learning going when schools close.
include: computers, tablets and internet connectivity in schools
digital learning platforms and educational content
radio, television and online remote learning
digital skills of learners
exclude: e-government services and digital public infrastructure, which belong to digital government & open data in the political dimension
broadband networks and internet use outside schools, which belong to digital connectivity & digital economy in the economic dimension
education delivered as part of a humanitarian response, which belongs to humanitarian needs & response in the humanitarian concerns, law & rights dimension
school buildings and electricity supply, which belong to school infrastructure & learning environment
questions: How did students' use of computers, tablets or online learning platforms change?
How many schools were connected to the internet or equipped with computers or tablets?
How did students keep learning during school closures, for example through radio, television, online or take-home lessons?
What effect of education technology or online learning on student achievement is reported?

outcomes.statement: Schools, teachers and learners receive devices, connectivity and digital or broadcast learning content.

indicators.name: Learning devices provided
indicators.question: How many computers, laptops or tablets were provided to schools, teachers or students?

indicators.name: Schools connected to the internet
indicators.question: How many schools were connected to the internet for teaching and learning?

indicators.name: Digital or broadcast learning content developed
indicators.question: Which digital learning content, platforms or broadcast lessons were developed, for example an online learning platform, e-textbooks, or radio or television lessons?

outcomes.statement: Learners and teachers use digital tools and remote learning regularly.

indicators.name: Students reached by remote learning
indicators.question: How many students, as a count or a share, were reached by or took part in radio, television, online or other remote lessons?

indicators.name: Use of digital learning tools
indicators.question: How much do students or teachers use the digital platforms, devices or content, for example active users, logins or hours of use?

indicators.name: Change in students per device
indicators.question: How did the number of students per computer or tablet, or the share of students with a device or internet access at home, change?

outcomes.statement: Digital learning is part of the education system, learners gain digital skills and learning continues through disruptions.

indicators.name: Change in learners' digital skills
indicators.question: How did the share of students or young people with basic digital or ICT skills change?

indicators.name: Learning effect of education technology
indicators.question: What change in student test scores or learning is attributed to the use of education technology or remote learning?

indicators.name: Stage of the digital or remote learning strategy
indicators.question: How far did a national or district strategy for digital education or for remote learning during school closures get?

categories.name: Education governance, financing & management
categories.definition: Changes in how education systems are planned, financed, monitored and held to account, from the ministry and district down to school management.
include: education sector plans and reforms
education budgets, school grants and spending per student
education management information systems and school data
school accountability, inspection, closure and school choice
exclude: public finance across government, which belongs to public finance & budget management in the political dimension
teacher recruitment, training and pay policy, which belong to teachers & school leadership
funding targeted at disadvantaged learners, which belongs to equity & inclusion in education
questions: How did public spending on education change, for example as a share of the budget or per student?
Which education sector plan, strategy or reform was prepared or adopted by the ministry or district?
What happened to low-performing schools, for example improvement plans, restructuring, takeover or closure?
How does the ministry or district collect and use school data, for example through an education management information system or a school census?

outcomes.statement: Education plans, data systems and school management structures are set up.

indicators.name: Education sector plan prepared
indicators.question: Was an education sector plan, education strategy or district education plan prepared or updated?

indicators.name: Education data system set up or improved
indicators.question: Which education management information systems, school censuses or student information systems were set up or improved?

indicators.name: School management committees set up or trained
indicators.question: How many school management committees, school boards or parent-teacher associations were set up or trained?

outcomes.statement: Schools receive and manage funds, plan their improvement, and education data are used for decisions.

indicators.name: Schools receiving school grants
indicators.question: How many schools, as a count or a share, received capitation, operating or school improvement grants?

indicators.name: Schools implementing improvement plans
indicators.question: How many schools, as a count or a share, carried out a school improvement or development plan?

indicators.name: Education data used for planning
indicators.question: Are education data, such as school census or assessment results, used to allocate resources or plan, for example in annual sector reviews or district plans?

outcomes.statement: Education is adequately financed and the system is managed for results.

indicators.name: Change in education's share of public spending
indicators.question: How did public education spending change as a share of total government spending or of GDP?
